title: Empty Review, Due today and Assignments are dead ends with zero rows and placeholder panels
detail: On a new account: Review's 'Today so far' prints Reviewed 0 / Accuracy — / Time 0 min (supporting zeros, invariant 77) and 'Next 7 days · nothing scheduled' keeps a 100px empty chart with seven grey ticks. Due today is one line ('Queue clear…') under a lone '← Queue' button on an otherwise empty 1210px page, with no way forward (e.g. 'Study a new topic' / Continue from the plan). Assignments shows four filter selects with nothing to filter and a right column whose only content is 'Select an assignment to see its brief…' although there are none.
evidence: shots/study-core/q-empty-review-mac.png, q-empty-due-mac.png, q-empty-assignments-mac.png; js/modules/due.js:222-236 (Today so far always drawn).
fix: Hide 'Today so far' until something was reviewed today and collapse the empty forecast to its sub-line; give Due today's empty state the next action from KOS.homeFocusPlan / Continue; hide the assignment filters and the detail column while the list is empty and let the empty state with its 'New assignment' button take the width.
rootCause: empty states render the populated layout's scaffolding

title: New assignment: a missing title is reported only in a toast; the field is not marked or focused, and a subject-less assignment can never be focused on
detail: Pressing Save with an empty title keeps the dialog open and shows the toast 'An assignment needs a title.', but the Title input gets no aria-invalid, no inline message and no focus (on the iPhone sheet the toast can sit under the keyboard). The form also allows 'No subject' (the default), and the detail panel then omits '◉ Focus on this' (it requires a.subject), so that assignment can never receive Focus time. The sheet's inputs are 39-42px tall on touch.
evidence: shots/study-core/q-asg-new-iphone.png; eval --size iphone: after Save, title aria-invalid null, activeElement not the title, #toast text 'An assignment needs a title.'; field heights 39-42. js/modules/assignments.js:316 (Focus button only when a.subject).
fix: Mark the field (aria-invalid + aria-describedby to an inline error) and focus it; either require a subject or let Focus run on a subject-less assignment (Focus's own subject picker); raise sheet controls to --hit-coarse.
rootCause: validation via toast only; Focus link gated on subject

title: KOS.rerender() never keeps the scroll position: it saves #main.scrollTop but #stage is the scroller, so every cloud pull jumps the page to the top
detail: KOS.rerender (the cloud-pull/background redraw path) reads and restores document.getElementById('main').scrollTop, but the element that actually scrolls is #stage (#main has overflow visible; on the iPad #main.scrollHeight 2406 vs #stage 2406/1120 scrolling). KOS.show then empties #main, the height collapses and the browser clamps #stage.scrollTop to 0. Repro (seeded account): open compsci 4.5.2.1, set #stage.scrollTop=900, KOS.rerender() -> 0. Same on Home (700 -> 0) and the Anime vault (1500 -> 0) at mac, ipad and iphone sizes. So any pull, merge, auto-ticked habit, Daily Review close etc. throws the reader back to the top of the page.
evidence: harness eval sd3.js: ipad {st1:900,st2:0,h1:700,h2:0,a1:1500,a2:0}; mac {st1:530,st2:0,...}; iphone same. Code: js/core/ui.js:353-356 (var main=getElementById('main'); var top=main.scrollTop; ... main.scrollTop=top); KOS.show resets main.scrollTop=0 at js/core/ui.js:1526
fix: Save/restore the real scroller (#stage, or a KOS.shell.scroller() helper that returns the element whose overflow scrolls, including the phone shell) and restore AFTER the view has rendered (and once more after async content lands, e.g. on next rAF / after vault lazy batch). Better: part of the redraw policy below — background redraws should not happen while the user is reading.
rootCause: rerender measured the wrong element after the shell moved scrolling to #stage

title: CS/Maths/IT notes reset to page 1 on every background redraw (the reported 'notes page 4 jumps back to page 1')
detail: In a subject topic the current note page lives in a closure variable (`var notePage = 0` inside the topic view). KOS.rerender re-runs the view, so the variable is recreated at 0. hub.js keeps only the open TAB across a redraw (openTabMemo), not the page. Repro on iPad: open compsci 4.5.2.1, Next page x3 -> 'Page 4 of 7', KOS.rerender() -> 'Page 1 of 7'. Code, Japanese, Mind and Creatives lessons do NOT have this bug because they store the page in state.ui.<space>.page[ref].
evidence: harness eval: {before:'Page 4 of 7', after:'Page 1 of 7'} at --size ipad. js/modules/hub.js:2901 (var notePage = 0), :2983 (cur = o.keep ? notePage : 0), :2590 (only the tab survives KOS.ui.redrawing). Contrast js/modules/codetopic.js:342/377, jatopic.js:206/229, crtopic.js:154/171, mindtopic.js:261/282 (ui.page[ref])
fix: Keep the note page in a module-level memo keyed by sid:ref (like openTabMemo) or per device in state.ui.notePage[sid:ref], and read it when KOS.ui.redrawing (and arguably on return to the topic). Same pattern the study spaces already use.
rootCause: transient reader state held in a view-render closure

title: A background redraw mid-flashcards restarts the set at card 1 and silently drops the cards already rated from the session ledger (no XP, no streak credit)
detail: The flashcard engine keeps queue, graduated and counts in its mount closure, and only logs the review session in finish(). A KOS.rerender mid-set remounts it: on a topic's Flashcards tab the queue is rebuilt from ALL the topic's cards, so the learner is put back on card 1 and re-meets cards they just rated (re-rating them applies FSRS's short-term rule again, skewing their schedule); on Due today the counts reset ('This session: 0 again · 0 hard · 3 good' -> ''), and because a session is only logged at finish(), the ratings made before the redraw never produce a session entry — their XP/gold and the study-streak credit are lost (the SRS schedule itself was saved). Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.2.1 Flashcards, rate 3 Good ('15 left of 18'), KOS.rerender() -> '18 left of 18', first card again. Due today: rate 3 ('304 left of 307', life line 3 good) -> after rerender '304 left of 304', life line empty.
evidence: harness eval (ipad): topic log ['18 left of 18 What is a number base?', ..., '15 left of 18'] -> afterFront '18 left of 18 What is a number base?'; due {d3life:'This session: 0 again · 0 hard · 3 good · 0 easy', dAfterLife:''}. js/engines/flashcards.js:295-322 (rate keeps counts in closure, store.save only), :325-355 (finish is the only KOS.sessions.log), :356 restart
fix: (1) Never redraw under an active study session (redraw policy below). (2) Keep an in-progress review session in a per-device session store (state.ui.fcSession[deckKey] = {queue keys, graduated, counts, startedAt}) and resume it on remount. (3) Log/bank the partial batch on unmount/pagehide (like Focus banks its clock, invariant 4c) so pay never depends on the DOM surviving.
rootCause: session progress and the pay-at-finish rule live in DOM-bound closures

title: Quiz progress and a typed exam answer are wiped by any background redraw
detail: Topic Quiz (MCQ) and Exam tabs keep the question index, chosen answers and typed text in engine closures. Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.2.1 Quiz, answer two -> 'Question 3 of 11'; KOS.rerender() -> 'Question 1 of 11' (tab kept, progress lost). Exam tab: go to 'Question 3 of 14', type into the answer textarea, KOS.rerender() -> 'Question 1 of 14' and the textarea is empty: the typed answer is lost with no recovery.
evidence: harness eval sd1.js (ipad): {quizBefore:'Question 3 of 11', quizAfter:'Question 1 of 11', examBefore:'Question 3 of 14', examTA:true, examAfter:'Question 1 of 14', examTAAfter:''}. js/engines/quiz.js:62-121 (MCQ state in closure), :225-232 (exam 'at' index in closure); js/modules/hub.js:3044-3084 remounts them
fix: Persist the quiz/exam position and drafts per device (state.ui.quizRun[sid:ref] = {at, picks, drafts}) like Code drafts, and restore on remount; plus the redraw policy (no background redraw while a study engine is mounted and touched).
rootCause: engine state in closures + unconditional rerender

title: Every cloud pull/merge redraws the active view unconditionally — even when nothing the view shows changed, and even while the user is mid-task
detail: cloudsync.rerenderCurrent() calls KOS.rerender() after every applied remote state: the clean path (applyRemoteState, cloudsync.js:775), the merge path (mergeRemoteIn, :495, also used by a push that lost its compare-and-set race, :533-560) and first link (:1279). There is no check of whether the merged document differs in anything the current view reads, no check that the user is interacting, a dialog/menu is open, an input has focus, or a study engine is running. The only guard in KOS.rerender is the ink pen (ui.js:347). Triggers that reach it: another device's push -> Realtime 'changed' (1.5 s debounce, :1483); returning to the app (visibilitychange/focus, :1548-1552, at most once a minute) — on the iPad every app switch; the 15-min interval; and the iPad's OWN ratings: each store.save -> noteChange -> push after 4 s -> if the Mac/iPhone pushed meanwhile the CAS fails -> conflict() -> mergeRemoteIn -> rerender. An idle open Mac pushes on its own (achievement sweep every 30 min, goals/notify ticks, routine auto-ticks, Daily Review words), so the iPad is redrawn under the user regularly. This is the root of the reported iPad resets.
evidence: js/core/cloudsync.js:487-497 (mergeRemoteIn -> rerenderCurrent), :723-733 (rerenderCurrent -> KOS.rerender), :773-777, :533-560 (conflict path), :1447-1459 (noteChange push), :1480-1495 (Realtime), :1541-1553 (interval/visible/focus); js/core/ui.js:344-357 (rerender: only inkUI.busy guard). Harness: KOS.rerender() reproduces every reset in the other findings.
fix: Systemic redraw policy: (1) cloudsync passes what changed (top-level keys that differ between pre- and post-merge state, cheap JSON compare per key) to KOS.rerender({changed:[...], background:true}); views declare the state keys they read (KOS.views.x.reads = ['srs','edits',...]) and are skipped when untouched. (2) A background redraw is DEFERRED while the page is 'busy': a dialog or menu open, focus in an input/textarea/contenteditable, a study engine mounted and touched in the last N minutes (flashcards/quiz/exam/japanese session/code task), pointer down, or within 30 s of the last interaction — instead show a quiet 'Updated on another device · Refresh' chip, and redraw on the next navigation. (3) For views that must refresh live, give them a refresh(changed) hook that patches in place instead of a full remount.
devices: iPad primarily (app switching + Pencil study), all
rootCause: full remount used as the generic refresh for background state changes, with no busy/changed gating

title: Closing the Daily Review sheet (Later, Esc, Close) redraws the page underneath — and on the iPad it can auto-open over a lesson when you return to the app
detail: reviewSheet.close() calls KOS.rerender() whenever it is not silent (dayreview.js:92), as does the final Close button (:661) and Skip (:709). The overlay is outside #main, so the page under it never needed a redraw; the redraw resets notes page, flashcards, quiz, scroll. Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.4.3 notes page 4 ('Page 4 of 7'), KOS.reviewSheet.open(slot), close -> 'Page 1 of 7' (screenshot). Worse, maybeOpen() runs on every visibilitychange to visible (:749); the deep-link guard uses bootHash, which is cleared 1.5 s after boot (:746), so after boot the sheet auto-opens over ANY page (a topic, a Code lesson, Due today) when the iPad app is brought back inside a new review slot; the blocked() check knows only Focus, a dialog and the Exam Room. Dismissing it then wipes the lesson state.
evidence: shots/sync-disruption/review-close-notes-reset.png (Page 1 of 7 after close; was Page 4 of 7). eval sd8.js {before:'Page 4 of 7', open:true, after:'Page 1 of 7'}. js/modules/dayreview.js:85-93, :661, :709, :722-729 (blocked), :744-749
fix: Close should repaint only what the review changed (chip, Home's cards if Home is on screen) — or call the policy's refresh(changed) — never a full remount. Auto-open on visibility should only happen on Home (or when no study page/engine is active); elsewhere it waits in the chip.
rootCause: overlay close uses KOS.rerender as a blanket refresh; auto-open guard only considers boot deep links

title: Handwritten tab Side by side: both panes jump to the top on a background redraw (1.5 s after the pen lifts)
detail: The ink guard in KOS.rerender only waits while inkUI.busy() (a stroke or text box open, or ink in the last 1.5 s). Once the pen has been lifted for 1.5 s — i.e. while the student reads the notes pane or thinks — a pull redraws the tab and both independent scroll regions reset. Repro iPad landscape (1180x820): compsci 4.5.4.3, Handwritten, Side by side; ink.side-notes scrolled to 600 and ink.side-page to 238; KOS.rerender() -> both 0. The notebook page-in-view and the notes position are lost, exactly the 'jumps back to the start' symptom on the iPad.
evidence: eval sd11.js (ipadl): {scrollers:['ink.side-notes 7882/744','ink.side-page 982/744'], before:[600,238], after:['ink.side-notes 0','ink.side-page 0']}. js/core/ui.js:347-351 (busy guard only), js/core/inkui.js:341
fix: Remember scroll of every [data-scroll-keep]/pane scroller (extend noteScrolls, ui.js:686, to vertical scrollTop for declared panes) and restore after render; better, defer background redraws while the Handwritten tab is open at all (ink pages and notes never change from a state pull — inksync updates pages itself).
devices: iPad landscape (Side by side is >1080 only)
rootCause: rerender only preserves horizontal scroller memos and the (wrong) #main scrollTop

title: A background redraw steals focus from whatever is being typed in — the iPad/iPhone keyboard closes mid-sentence
detail: KOS.rerender remounts #main; the focused field is destroyed and focus falls to <body>. The quick-note draft itself survives (stored per device), but the caret is gone, so on the iPad the on-screen keyboard dismisses while the user is typing; any keystrokes in flight are lost. The same applies to every inline input on any page (search filters in vaults, Money amount fields, Goals editor in-page fields, Code task editor, Writing Desk). Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.4.3, focus the quick note, type, caret at 4, KOS.rerender() -> document.activeElement BODY; the new textarea has the text but no focus (selection at end).
evidence: eval (ipad): {active:'BODY ', val:'half a thou', sel:11}. js/core/ui.js:344-357, :1520-1541 (main.innerHTML = '' then remount); js/core/a11y.js:97 comment says a redraw must leave the reader where they are but there is no focus restore
fix: Policy: never run a background redraw while document.activeElement is an editable element inside #main (defer until blur + idle). As a fallback, record a focus signature (data-ui + index + selection) before the redraw and restore it after (mobile-shell.js:600-640 already has calendarFocusSignature to generalise).
rootCause: remount without focus/selection preservation

title: Japanese review/learn session restarts and loses its unlogged results on a background redraw
detail: KOS.jaRun.run keeps `results` and the index in its closure and pays only at the end (KOS.ja.finishSession(results)). A KOS.rerender on #/japanese/session/... re-runs run(): the list is rebuilt from KOS.ja.due() (facets already graded drop out) and the results so far are discarded, so the +1 XP per passed facet for them is never logged. Mind's Daily 15 does it right: its d.results are saved in state and logged once (mind.js:594/662).
evidence: js/modules/jarun.js:361-390 (run, `var results = [], i = 0`), :434 (finishSession only at end); js/modules/japanese.js:305 (view calls run on every render); contrast js/modules/mind.js:594,662
fix: Keep the running session (keys, index, results) per device in state.ui.japanese.run and resume on remount, or bank results incrementally; plus the redraw policy.
rootCause: session state in closure + pay at finish

title: A background redraw closes any open menu or popover — including the header bell, which is outside the page
detail: KOS.show always calls closeOpenMenu(false) before drawing, also for a redraw (_nav). So a pull arriving while the notifications popover, a Filters menu or a ⋯ menu is open makes it vanish under the finger. Repro: Home, open the bell (menu .k-menu-panel.k-nt-pop present), KOS.rerender() -> menu gone.
evidence: eval sd6.js (ipad): {menuOpen:true, menuCls:'k-menu-panel k-nt-pop', menuAfter:false}. js/core/ui.js:1513-1519 (closeOpenMenu before every render)
fix: On a redraw (KOS.ui.redrawing) keep a menu whose anchor is outside #main, and for menus inside #main defer the background redraw while a menu is open (redraw policy).
rootCause: navigation clean-up applied to redraws

title: Edits in a Code lesson's runnable listings are lost on a background redraw
detail: A Code lesson's notes listings are editable (code.editor-input) so the learner can experiment, but their text is not kept anywhere; task editors save drafts (debounced 400 ms, state.ui.code.drafts) and survive. Repro iPad: code 1.1, type into the three listing editors, wait 900 ms, KOS.rerender() -> all three back to the shipped code (the quick-note textarea survives).
evidence: eval sd5.js: {n:4, where:['code.editor-input'x3,'topic.quick-note'], kept:[false,false,false,true]}. js/modules/code.js:629-632 (only tasks call setDraft); js/core/code.js:612-621
fix: Keep listing edits as drafts too (key `listing:<lesson>:<i>`, cleared by 'Reset'), or defer redraws while an editor has focus.
rootCause: listing editor state only in the DOM

title: routines.onSession redraws the whole page whenever an auto-tracked habit ticks itself — e.g. right after a flashcard batch or Code task pass
detail: Every logged session (flashcard batch finish, exam item marked, Code task pass, Japanese session) calls routines.onSession, which runs autoSync() and, if any auto-tracked habit ticked, KOS.rerender() (only guarded against an open dialog). So the moment a 'Review 20 cards' or '1 Code task passed' habit completes, the page that caused it is remounted: the flashcards 'Session complete' summary is replaced by a fresh deck, a Code task's passing result panel is redrawn, an exam tab returns to question 1. Only the habit chip/Home needs to change.
evidence: js/core/routines.js:697-700 (onSession -> autoSync -> KOS.rerender), :672-690 (autoSync), js/engines/flashcards.js:349 (session logged at finish), js/engines/quiz.js:428 (exam item logs a session). Not reproduced end-to-end in the harness (could not get an auto habit to tick with a hand-made ledger entry); path read from code.
fix: Replace the blanket rerender with a 'routines changed' event that Home/Routines/the header chip listen to; never remount a study view for it.
rootCause: blanket rerender as change notification

title: Toasts are capped at half the viewport width and, on the iPhone, sit on top of the flashcard rating buttons (and catch taps when they carry Undo)
detail: #toast is positioned with inset-inline-start:50% + translate(-50%), so its shrink-to-fit width is limited to the space right of the centre line: 201 px on the iPhone (402/2) and 410 px on the iPad (820/2). A one-line message wraps to four lines (98 px tall). On the iPhone it sits 12 px above the tab bar, i.e. exactly over the Hard/Good rating buttons of a flashcard (toast 101,708 201x98 vs rate row 16,694 370x60: overlapping), and an action toast has pointer-events:auto, so a rating tap lands on the toast. Flashcards themselves raise toasts mid-set (leech, 'Type your answer first').
evidence: shots/sync-disruption/toast-over-rate-iphone.png; eval sd10.js iphone {toast:[101,708,201,98], rate:[16,694,370,60], overlap:true, pe:'auto'}, ipad {toast:[205,1092,410,64]}. css/components.css:389-408, :669
fix: Centre with inset-inline:0; margin-inline:auto; inline-size:fit-content (keep max-inline-size), and on study pages lift the toast above the active control row (or place it top-centre on phones while a study engine is mounted).
rootCause: left:50% shrink-to-fit width; fixed bottom offset ignores page controls

title: A redraw mid-retrieval resets the Code retrieval card's tries, hint flag and clock, so the derived grade comes out better than earned
detail: Code retrieval grades are derived from tries, hints and time (invariant 107, never self-reported), but the card keeps `started`, `tries` and `hinted` in its render closure. After a failed try and an opened hint, a background redraw remounts the card with tries=0, hinted=false and a fresh clock; passing then records a clean, fast first-try grade and schedules the card too far out. Task timers (code.js:601) reset the same way.
evidence: js/modules/code.js:972 (var started = Date.now(), tries = 0, hinted = false), :984 (clock), :601-611 (task clock). Code-read; the remount path is the same KOS.rerender reproduced in the other findings.
fix: Keep the in-progress attempt (tries, hinted, startedAt) per card in state.ui.code.attempt[key] until it is graded, and defer background redraws while a retrieval is open.
rootCause: evidence inputs held in closures

title: After a background redraw the open dialog's opener is detached, so closing it drops focus to <body>
detail: Dialogs survive a redraw (they live on body), but KOS.ui.openDialog restores focus to the opener, which the redraw replaced. Repro: Assignments, '＋ New assignment', type a title, KOS.rerender() (dialog and text survive), Cancel -> document.activeElement is BODY; the keyboard/VoiceOver user is thrown to the top of the document. cloudsync does not check for an open dialog (routines.onSession does).
evidence: eval sd7.js: {dlgAfter:true, inpAfter:'Typed title', openerConnected:false, focusAfterClose:'BODY'}. js/core/routines.js:699 has the dialog guard; js/core/cloudsync.js:723-733 has none
fix: Defer background redraws while KOS.ui.topDialog() (policy), and in openDialog's restore fall back to an element with the same data-ui/text in the new DOM (as mobile-shell's calendarFocusSignature already does, mobile-shell.js:620-640).
rootCause: redraw under an open dialog

title: Boot-time redraws of whatever page the PWA reopened on (Google read-only copy, own art pictures, sample seed)
detail: Three boot paths call KOS.rerender() on the current page after async work: KOS.ext boot when Google Calendar is connected (ext.js:364, after loadRo from IndexedDB), KOS.art.loadOwn (main.js:307) and the sample seed (main.js:299-304). The iPad Home Screen app restores the last route (e.g. a topic), so the page the user has just started reading or tapping is remounted a moment after launch, for data (Google's read-only chips, decorative art) that only Calendar or a painted slot needs.
evidence: js/core/ext.js:364; js/main.js:299-307
fix: Have these refresh only the views that read them (Calendar for loadRo; the art slots via KOS.art.apply/paint, which artslot.js already does in place) instead of a full remount.
rootCause: KOS.rerender used as a broadcast

title: Inconsistent refresh policy: Google/Todoist pulls change Calendar and Reminders without redrawing them, while a state pull redraws every page
detail: KOS.ext.syncAll (every cycle and the 1.5 s 'soon' sync) writes pulled events and reminders through the owners, then only notifies KOS.ext.onChange listeners — only the Connections page listens. An open Calendar or Reminders page keeps showing the old data (a task completed in Todoist stays unticked on screen) until the user navigates, whereas a cloud state pull remounts any page however unrelated. There is no single 'state changed → which views care' mechanism.
evidence: js/core/ext.js:325-337 (syncAll -> changed()), :294; js/modules/connections.js:173-177 (the only listener); js/core/extgcal.js and exttasks.js contain no redraw
fix: Introduce one change bus (KOS.changed(domains)) fired by cloudsync (with the keys that differed), ext, routines, inksync, files; views subscribe by domain and refresh in place (or defer while busy).
rootCause: no domain-scoped change notification

title: Specification tab shows garbled PDF-extraction text on most Maths leaves (M7.3 included)
detail: The Spec tab is drawn from js/data/maths.js content/info lines, which are raw, broken PDF extraction. Examples: M7.3 guidance reads "v = u + at r = ut +1at2 / e.g. , with vectors / 2 given in i - j or column vector form". 5.6 reads "Understand and use double a n g le f / rm u l a e ; u s e / f s in ( A ± B ), fo r m u l a e fo r / ± ± cos (A B)". 2.1 reads "× = , ÷ = - , = m n n am / The equivalence ofa and should be known." 2.10 starts mid-sentence: "into partial fractions". 25 leaves still contain the extraction artefact "need to learn:" or "students need to learn:". A heuristic found fragment lines in 36 of the 89 leaves: 1.1 2.1 2.2 2.3 2.4 2.5 2.7 2.9 3.3 4.1 4.2 4.3 5.1 5.2 5.3 5.5 5.6 5.7 6.2 6.3 6.4 7.1 7.2 7.4 8.2 8.3 8.5 8.6 9.4 10.4 S2.3 S4.1 S5.3 M7.4 M8.3 M8.6, and reading the dump shows more. Exponents, fractions, sums and integrals are lost throughout. This is very likely part of why M7.3 looks bare.
evidence: shots/content-maths/m73-spec-mac.png; shots/content-maths/p5-6-spec-mac.png; cm/spine.txt (every leaf's spec text); tools/gen_data.py:240-255 (maths_group copies clean(x) of the extracted lines)
fix: Hand-author the 89 Maths spec entries from the Edexcel 9MA0 PDF as typeset blocks (LaTeX in $…$). Either fix the extractor or add a checked-in override table that gen_data.py applies (as SHORT does), and regenerate. Drop the "need to learn:" headers. Add a smoke test that refuses fragment lines (≤4 characters, runs of single letters, "need to learn").
rootCause: The spec spine is generated from a PDF text extraction (/home/claude/extract) that splits equations and kerned headings, and no override or cleanup pass exists for Maths.

title: Quiz answers are almost always A or B, and options are never shuffled
detail: Of 1,058 Maths quiz items, the correct option is A in 531 and B in 481. Only 44 are C and 2 are D. Base files: 380 A, 100 B, 17 C, 1 D. Bank files: 151 A, 381 B, 27 C, 1 D. KOS.quiz.mountMCQ renders opts in authored order, and its Shuffle button only reorders the questions. A learner soon learns to pick A on a base item or B on a bank item, so the quiz score stops measuring understanding. Separately, the correct option is uniquely the longest in 317 items (30%).
evidence: cm/metrics.json ansDist per leaf; js/engines/quiz.js:66 (Shuffle shuffles order only), :88-96 (item.opts rendered in order, answer compared to item.ans at :113); e.g. js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js:305-306 (every item ans: 0); shots/content-maths/m73-quiz-ipad.png (Q1 answer A)
fix: In mountMCQ, shuffle a per-question option permutation at mount and on Retry, seeded per attempt, and map clicks back to the original index so the stats and the why text stay valid. Optionally also rebalance the authored ans positions so a fixed order is fair too.
rootCause: Authors put the right answer first (bank authors second), and the engine trusts the authored order.

title: "Write it out" chip overlaps worked-example titles on every device and is only 23px tall
detail: On worked cards with more than one step, the "Write it out" pill is position:absolute at the top-right, and the .k-n-worked-head row reserves no room for it. On M7.3's notes it lies over the title or src text on 4 of 15 cards on the Mac (1470), 2 of 15 on iPad portrait, 3 of 15 on iPad landscape and 9 of 15 on iPhone (402). Example on the Mac: "Write it out" is printed over "AS Specimen · P2 Q1(a)(b) · 5 marks". On iPhone it covers "Find the initial velocity". The pill measures 81×23 px with min-block-size:0, below the 44px touch minimum (invariant 69). The same overlap affects every subject's worked cards, because content.js is shared.
evidence: shots/content-maths/writeout-overlap-mac.png; shots/content-maths/m73-notes-p6-iphone.png; measured: btn rect [233,618,81,23] while .k-n-worked-head starts at y=626, width 334 (iphone); css/views/ink.css:300; js/core/content.js:373; css/views/study.css:346
fix: Put the chip in the head's flex flow (margin-inline-start:auto, before Copy) instead of absolute positioning, or give the head padding-inline-end equal to the chip's and Copy's widths. Raise the hit area to 44px for coarse pointers.
rootCause: An absolutely positioned control added onto a flex header that wraps freely.

title: A curriculum fork silently hides later curriculum upgrades (plausible cause of "M7.3 is basically bare")
detail: KOS.content.get and srs read state.edits first (invariant 86). A fork copies the shipped material at the moment of the first edit and is never compared with the curriculum again. M7.3 was an outline entry until commit 4d791ca ("load M6–M7 at depth, drop their outline entries"), and a9f64b5 rewrote M7.2 and M7.3. A Notes fork made before then (or one carried over from S7.3 by the ref rename, router.js:117 renamedRef) keeps showing the old, thin outline notes. Nothing tells the user that a newer, much deeper version exists. The only sign is the Edit button's data-state forked (hub.js:2828). The shipped M7.3 renders in full (8 pages), so a bare M7.3 on the user's device most likely comes from such a fork.
evidence: js/core/edits.js:1-60 (no base hash or staleness check: grep for stale/baseHash finds nothing); git log -- js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js (a9f64b5, 4d791ca); shots/content-maths/m73-mac.png (shipped content present)
fix: Record a hash of the shipped kind on each fork (fork.base). When the shipped hash differs, show a banner on the tab: "The curriculum for this topic was updated after you edited it: View new · Keep mine · Merge (append your rows)". Check the user's real state for state.edits.topics['maths:M7.3'] (or 'maths:S7.3').
rootCause: The fork model has no notion of the base version it was taken from.

title: Bank files duplicate base flashcards and quiz items in the same leaf (17 exact repeats, about 45 same-answer groups)
detail: bank-maths-*.js were added without a duplicate check against the base items. Exact repeats in the same quiz include: 2.1 "$8^{2/3}$ =" (qz0 and qz8); 4.1 "$\binom92$" (qz0 and qz18), "Coefficient of $x$ in $(2+x)^5$" (qz8 and qz22), "Coefficient of $x^2$ in $(1+x)(1+4x+6x^2)$" (qz10 and qz24), "$(1+3x)^{-1}$ valid for" (qz4 and qz20); 5.2 "$\sin3\theta\approx$" and "$1-\cos2\theta\approx$" both twice; 5.3 "$\tan\frac{3\pi}4$" twice; 5.6 "$\cos(A-B)$" twice; 6.3 "$\log_{10}0.001$" twice; 2.6 "$(x-2)$ is a factor means" twice; 2.8 "inverse only if one-to-one" twice; 7.2 "$d/dx\sqrt x$" twice. Flashcard and quiz pairs on the same fact: M7.3 "Which equation has no t?" (fc1 and qz10, and qz1 again); M7.5 time of flight and greatest height; 8.5 "∫ln x"; 7.5 "d/dx(3y²)"; 3.3 parametric dy/dx; 10.3 midpoint; 8.1 states the FTC twice (fc0 and fc5b) and uses the same f′ setup twice (fc4 and fc6b); 6.1 has "$e^{2x}=5$" as fc10b and qz3, "features of $a^x$" as fc0 and fc7b, and the asymptotes of $e^x+3$ and $e^x+2$ as qz0 and qz6b; 10.4 has "|AC| = 4 with one unknown" three times. Cross-leaf: S4.2 and S4.3 repeat continuity-correction cards, and S4.1 and S5.2 repeat "$P(X\ge k)$ in cumulative form". Full list: cm/dups2.json (66 within-leaf pairs, 14 cross-leaf pairs, 45 same-answer groups).
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/dups2.json; e.g. js/data/content/maths-pure-p8.js:505 vs bank-maths-pure-c.js:457 ("Before integrating x²/(x−1) you should")
fix: Delete or replace the bank items flagged in dups2.json with new item shapes. Add a smoke test that canonicalises q and the answer (\dfrac→\frac, strip spaces) and fails on an exact or same-answer duplicate inside one leaf. Removing flashcards must follow invariant 87 (carry the original index as a third element).
rootCause: KOS.content.extend concatenates bank arrays blindly, and no test checks for duplicates.

title: Thin notes on core Pure and Applied leaves (depth very uneven: 200 to 8,700 words)
detail: Base notes (before the bank's past-paper page), as approximate words / pages / worked examples: 8.4 Integration as a limit of a sum 204/1/2; 8.1 Fundamental Theorem 258/1/2; 6.1 Exponential functions 331/2/2; 6.2 Gradient of e^kx 350/1/2 (no page breaks at all); 6.5 Solving a^x=b 401/2/4; 8.6 Integration with partial fractions 414/2/3; 4.3 Sigma 452/2/3; 4.6 Series in modelling 479/2/3 (no exam-tagged worked examples, so only 2 exam items); 7.2 Differentiating x^n, e^kx, trig, ln x 486/2/4; 6.3 Logarithms 489/2/4; M8.3 Weight 558/3/4 (3 exam items); 5.4 Reciprocal and inverse trig 563; S4.3 Selecting a distribution 587 (4 exam items); 8.8 617; 6.4 627; 3.4 632; 10.4 636/1/3; 8.2 Integrating standard functions 637; 9.5 773/1. The median leaf is about 1,040 words, and 4.1 has 8,667 words and 31 worked examples. 7.2 and 8.2 carry most of Paper 1 and 2 calculus but have the depth of a summary. Leaves with 5 or fewer exam items: 2.11 3.4 4.6 5.3 5.4 6.1 6.2 8.1 8.4 8.6 8.8 9.5 S4.3 M8.1 M8.3 M8.5.
evidence: cm/metrics.json; table printed by cm/metrics.js; shots/content-maths/p8-4-notes-mac.png (8.4 is one short page)
fix: Run the per-section depth pipeline used for 4.1, 2.x and M7 on P6 (6.1–6.5), P7.2, P8.1, 8.2, 8.4, 8.6, 8.8, 4.3, 4.6, 5.4, 10.4, 9.5, S4.3 and M8.3. Target at least 3 pages, at least 5 exam-tagged worked examples with Edexcel marks, a figure where a picture helps, and an exam toolkit page.
rootCause: The depth rewrite stopped short on P6 to P8 and several small leaves. The files for P1, P9, P10 and M7 to M9 are dated 8 October and P2 to P8 27 October, and the light leaves were never brought up to the contract.

title: Statistics and Mechanics leaf titles are cut-off 80-character spec sentences, unlike the short Pure titles
detail: Pure leaves have names like "Straight lines" and "Trapezium rule". Every S and M leaf is titled with the first 80 characters of its spec sentence plus "…", e.g. M7.3 "Understand, use and derive the formulae for constant acceleration for motion in …" and S4.1 "simple, discrete probability distributions" (lowercase fragment). The page title is then cut again to three lines with an ellipsis, the spine rows read "Understand and use the lang…" five times in a row under M7, and the search results and breadcrumbs show the same. gen_data.py already defines SHORT_S ("suvat (constant acceleration)", "Projectiles", …), but it is never applied to the checked-in maths.js. Its keys are bare ("7.3") while the payload's refs are "S1.1" and "M7.3", and the generator cannot run locally (it reads /home/claude/extract).
evidence: shots/content-maths/m73-mac.png (title and spine); shots/content-maths/m73-notes-iphone.png; tools/gen_data.py:249 (80-char truncation), :287-301 (SHORT_S and its lookup by c["ref"]); js/data/maths.js:989 ("S1.1"), :1287 ("M7.3")
fix: Key SHORT_S by the final refs (S1.1…S5.3, M6.1…M9.1) and add a payload-only pass, like --mech-refs, that applies titles to the checked-in maths.js. Then regenerate.
rootCause: The short-title table is keyed by refs that never match the stats and mech children, and the generator's source is not available to re-run.

title: Wrong flashcard answer: 9.3 Newton–Raphson from x0 = 0 gives x1 = −2.5, not 2.5
detail: 9.3 FC5 (bank) asks "Why does $x_0 = 0$ fail for $f(x)=x^3-2x-5$?" and answers "it does not fail here; $x_1 = 2.5$". In fact f(0) = −5 and f′(0) = −2, so x1 = 0 − (−5)/(−2) = −2.5, which the card's own formula (2x³+5)/(3x²−2) also gives. The question also states something false: it says the method fails and the answer says it does not.
evidence: js/data/content/bank-maths-pure-c.js:646
fix: Rewrite the card, e.g. "Where would NR fail for $f(x)=x^3-2x-5$?" → "Where $f'(x_0)=0$: $x_0=\pm\sqrt{2/3}$". Or keep the x0 = 0 example with "$x_1=-2.5$ (far from the root 2.09)". Keep its schedule key (invariant 87).
rootCause: An arithmetic sign slip in the bank author's answer, with no automated check on numeric answers.

title: Cards filed under the wrong leaf
detail: 6.1 (Exponential functions) holds solve-a^x=b items that belong to 6.5: fc3 "Solve $4^x=100$", fc10b "$e^{2x}=5$", fc13b "$2^x=20$", qz3. M8.3 (Weight and gravity) holds suvat projectile items that belong to M7.3: fc13b impact speed and fc14b rebound height. S4.3 (Selecting a distribution) holds normal-approximation and continuity-correction drill that belongs to S4.2: fc10b–fc14b, qz4b, qz5b, qz7b. 2.10 (Partial fractions) qz3 is an integral, ∫2/(x+1), which is 8.6's topic. 10.4 fc8b is an average-speed question. 8.1 fc9b ends without an answer ("a third condition is needed").
evidence: cm/load.js dumps; read with the node print script (outputs quoted in this audit); bank-maths-pure-*.js, bank-maths-mech.js, bank-maths-stats.js
fix: Move these items to their own leaves, keeping each card's original key as a whole-key third element (invariant 87), or replace them with items on the leaf's own skill.
rootCause: Bank items were grouped by past-paper question rather than by spec point.

title: "Past-paper patterns" pages are one wall-of-text paragraph
detail: 55 of the 57 note paragraphs over 60 words sit on the bank's "Past-paper patterns" page. That is one per leaf, up to 135 words of run-on text with bold phrases and inline series lists. This goes against the user's rule of short lines and bullets, not paragraphs. On M7.3 page 8, one 6-line paragraph lists every question shape, and the lower half of the page is empty. It also repeats the M7.3 overview table of question shapes on page 1.
evidence: shots/content-maths/m73-pastpaper-mac.png; js/data/content/bank-maths-*.js (each X(…) notes: [{page:"Past-paper patterns"}, "<long string>"]); counted by a script: 57 paragraphs over 60 words, 55 after the bank page
fix: Convert each to a {table:{head:[Question shape, Marks, Seen in]}} or a {ul} of one shape per line, or fold it into the leaf's existing overview table and drop the page.
rootCause: The bank files were written as prose summaries before the short-lines rule.

title: 29 leaves have no figure where a picture would teach
detail: Leaves with figs=0: 2.1 2.2 2.10 2.11 3.4 4.1 4.2 4.3 4.4 4.5 4.6 5.5 5.6 5.8 5.9 6.4 6.5 7.2 7.4 7.5 7.6 8.1 8.2 8.5 8.6 8.7 8.8 9.5 S3.3. Clear candidates: 5.9 Trig in context (Ferris wheel or tide curve), 5.6 R-form (the R·sin(θ+α) graph with max and min), 8.7 Separable DEs (family of solution curves, which the spec requires students to sketch), 3.4 Parametric modelling (motion path), 7.5 Implicit differentiation (circle with tangent), 4.2 Sequences (increasing, decreasing and periodic plots), 8.2 and 8.1 (antiderivative family), 2.11 modelling curves. Per the user's notes rule, annotated {fig} diagrams are expected wherever a picture helps.
evidence: cm/metrics.json figs column
fix: Add declarative {fig} diagrams (core/figures.js) to these leaves during the depth pass. They are SVG-declarative, so no raster art is needed.
rootCause: Figures were added only as each section was rewritten at depth.

title: Units such as "m s$^{-1}$" break across lines
detail: Units are authored as "m s$^{-1}$" with a normal space. At wrap points the line breaks inside the unit, leaving "…5 m s" at a line end and "−1" on the next line. Seen in M7.2's worked question in Dawn on the Mac ("travels at a constant 5 m s / −1 for the next 15 seconds").
evidence: shots/content-maths/m72-notes-dawn-mac.png
fix: Author units as a single KaTeX segment, e.g. $\text{m s}^{-1}$ or $5\ \text{m}\,\text{s}^{-1}$, or have inline() replace the space before a unit with U+00A0 and wrap the unit in a white-space:nowrap span.
rootCause: A breakable space plus a separate math segment for the exponent.

title: Two-option quiz items in a 4-option quiz
detail: 8.1 qz9 ("$\int_2^5 f = -\int_5^2 f$ is: true / false") and 4.5 qz12 have only two options, so a guess is right 50% of the time, and they look different from the other items.
evidence: cm/dups.json quizBad entries maths:8.1 #9 and maths:4.5 #12 (bank-maths-pure-c.js, bank-maths-pure-b.js)
fix: Rewrite them as 4-option items, or as flashcards.
rootCause: Bank authoring.

title: IT spec text for F206.6.1, F204.6.5, F202.5.1, F201.5.2, F200.5.3 (and F200.2.x/F202.2.x) holds garbled PDF dumps of the assessment criteria
detail: The generated IT spec (js/data/it.js) contains multi-thousand-character strings of shuffled PDF text in the Spec tab content/info lists for the last leaf of each unit: e.g. F206.6.1 'Ways to reflect' ends with a 2,271-char 'Lessons learnt Assessment criteria The table below gives...' string and a 2,884-char info item; F204.6.5 has 2,164/1,007/2,510-char strings; F202.5.1 2,330/538/2,502; F201.5.2 (the unit the user is sitting) has 'Urban and community planning Assessment guidance This unit is assessed by an exam...' and an 831-char run; F200.5.3 876 chars. Shorter merged rows also start with a dangling 'include:' (F200.2.2, F200.2.3, F200.2.6, F201.2.4, F202.2.2, F202.2.4, F202.2.5, F202.3.3). Column-interleaved words ('The tasks. means that the unit grade awarded') are unreadable on the Spec tab and pollute search and the Assistant's spec reads. F206 is the NEA the user is doing now. Beyond the long dumps, 189 short spec rows in 39 IT leaves are fragments ('□ Does', '□ Techniques To', '• Diagnostic Prescriptive □', a bare '□'), e.g. F201.2.3 Data mining techniques reads ['□ Data mining','□ Data mining techniques','• Descriptive','• Diagnostic Prescriptive □','□','□ Does','□'] and F201.2.6 omits 'Factor analysis' which the notes teach.
fix: Fix tools/gen_data.py's IT parser to stop each leaf at the 'Assessment criteria'/'Assessment guidance'/'Synoptic assessment' headings and at page-column breaks, and to join 'To include:' continuation lines into bullet rows; regenerate it.js (invariant 24) and add a smoke check that no IT spec string exceeds ~300 chars or starts with 'include:'.
rootCause: PDF parser in tools/gen_data.py appends trailing unit-level sections (criteria tables, guidance, synoptic tables) to the last topic leaf and mis-splits two-column 'To include' boxes.

title: IT spec has a duplicate leaf: F206.6.1 'Ways to reflect' and 'Overview of the assessment' share a ref, so 'Ways to reflect' cannot be opened
detail: F206 Topic Area 6 has two children with the SAME ref F206.6.1: 'Ways to reflect' and 'Overview of the assessment' (qualification-structure text: entry codes H019/H119, GLH). The spine lists both rows, but both resolve to one topic: opening F206.6.1 (either row) shows the title 'Overview of the assessment' and its Spec (entry codes, GLH), with the 'Ways to reflect' notes, flashcards and quiz underneath. The real 'Ways to reflect' spec (Boud, Keogh and Walker; effectiveness of processes and tools; lessons learnt) is unreachable, and progress, RAG, attachments and FSRS keys are shared by the two rows. F206 is the NEA the user is doing now. Also F201.5.3 'NEA Units' is an empty phantom leaf in it.js (hidden by the spine, which counts F201 as 15, but present for any reader of KOS_DATA).
evidence: js/data/it.js:2246 and :2285 both 'ref': 'F206.6.1'; js/data/it.js:946-950; audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/content-cs-it/it-f2061-spec-ipad.png (title 'Overview of the assessment', Notes 4 / Flashcards 14 are Ways to reflect's); eval on #cols: rows 'Ways to reflect F206.6.1' and 'Overview of the assessment F206.6.1', h1 after KOS.show('ref',{subject:'it',ref:'F206.6.1'}) = 'Overview of the assessment'
fix: In gen_data.py drop qualification-overview nodes ('Overview of the assessment', 'NEA Units') and assert ref uniqueness at generation; regenerate it.js; rename/prune any stored state keyed to F201.5.3 at the store gate like IT_NOT_TAKEN.
rootCause: Generator does not filter non-topic headings and has no uniqueness check on refs.

title: Quiz answers are guessable: the correct option is A or B in 94% of CS questions (D only 12 of 1,347) and options are never shuffled
detail: Across all 1,347 CS quiz questions the correct index is A 677, B 590, C 68, D 12; IT's 288 are A 17, B 211, C 57, D 3. The correct option is also the uniquely longest one in 688/1,347 CS (51%) and 201/288 IT (70%) questions, against ~25% by chance. KOS.quiz.mountMCQ renders item.opts in authored order (only the question order has a Shuffle), so a learner quickly learns 'pick A/B, pick the longest', and 'Quiz best' on the topic inspector and RAG overstate recall. 46 leaves have 60%+ of answers in one position (e.g. 4.4.1.3: 11 of 12 are A; 4.5.2.1 9/11 A).
evidence: node content-cs-it/quiz.js over dump.json: compsci [677,590,68,12], it [17,211,57,3]; longest-correct compsci 688/1347, it 201/288; js/engines/quiz.js:88 item.opts.forEach renders in authored order (shuffle at :25 is only applied to question order, :66)
fix: Shuffle each question's options at render with a deterministic per-question seed (map ans through the permutation; keep keyboard 1–4 on the displayed order) and rebalance the longest-option bias by trimming correct options or lengthening distractors in the authored banks; add a smoke check that no leaf has >50% of answers at one index after shuffling is off.
rootCause: Authoring habit (answer written first) plus an engine that never permutes options.

title: 'Write it out' pill on worked examples overlaps the example's title on iPhone and iPad
detail: The worked-example card's 'Write it out' button is absolutely positioned at a fixed inset from the top-right, so whenever the title runs that far it sits on top of the words. On iPhone 5 of 8 worked cards on 4.6.4.1 page 4 are covered ('The bottle-filling conveyor', 'Process X: circuit and expression', 'XOR without an XOR gate', 'Draw without simplifying', 'Only AND, OR and NOT'); on iPad portrait (820) 14 of 72 buttons across 4.6.4.1, 4.5.4.4, 4.10.4 and 4.7.3.5 overlap text, on the Mac 1 of 72. The pill is also 81×23 px, under the 44 px touch minimum (invariant 69).
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/content-cs-it/cs-4641-p3-iphone.png; eval at iphone: button rect x233 y824 w81 h23 position:absolute over title text; ipad hit 14/72, mac 1/72; css/views/ink.css:300 .k-n-writeout { position: absolute; inset-block-start: var(--sp-8); inset-inline-end: calc(var(--sp-8) * 9) }; js/core/content.js:373
fix: Put the button in the worked card's head row as a flex item (title flex:1, min-width:0; actions group with Copy), wrapping under the title below 560px; give it the touch minimum height on coarse pointers.
rootCause: Absolute positioning with a fixed inset instead of taking part in the header's layout.

title: Same past-paper question appears twice in a CS leaf's Exam questions (worked card + bank item): 202 duplicate groups across 88 of 131 leaves
detail: Each CS leaf's exam list = examFromWorked(notes) + bank-cs-*.js items concatenated by KOS.content.extend. The bank re-writes questions already authored as worked exam cards, so the learner meets the same AQA question twice in a row of practice, with different wording and differently formatted source labels ('AQA June 2025 · P1 Q01.1' vs 'AQA 2025 P1 Q1.1'). Example 4.2.6.1 Hash tables: items 1/6 (2025 P1 Q1.1), 2/5 (Q1.2), 3/7 (Q1.3); 4.6.1.4 has 'Describe two functions of an operating system.' twice verbatim (2022 P2 Q4.3). Worst leaves: 4.7.3.5 (7 groups), 4.2.2.1, 4.6.2.1 (5), 4.2.4.1, 4.2.6.1, 4.5.5.3, 4.5.6.7, 4.6.4.1, 4.7.3.2, 4.7.3.7, 4.8.1, 4.10.3 (4). Exam-question counts and 'Done exam questions' progress are inflated accordingly.
evidence: node script over dump.json keyed on year-paper-question: 202 groups, 88 leaves, 1194 items; js/core/content.js:515 extend() concatenates exam without de-duplication; js/core/content.js:546 builds 'AQA June …' src vs bank files' 'AQA 2025 P1 Q1.1'
fix: Drop the bank item when a worked card of the same leaf cites the same series/paper/question (do it in the bank files, or dedupe in extend() by a normalised src key), and normalise src labels to one format; add a smoke66 check for duplicate src within a leaf.
rootCause: Bank files were authored independently of the worked cards; extend() concatenates blindly.

title: Steps blocks in 4.5.x notes render prose as monospace code with literal **bold** and a redundant '1.' heading
detail: In 4.5.2.1 (Decimal → binary), 4.5.4.1, 4.5.4.3, 4.5.4.5, 4.5.6.4 and 4.5.6.7 the authored {steps} use h:'1.', h:'2.' (duplicating the numbered circle) and put prose with markdown in m. The renderer escapes m into a preformatted maths/code line, so the page shows '1.' next to circle 1 and a monospace box reading 'record the **remainder** (MOD)'. 21 numbered headings and 10 markdown-in-m steps.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/content-cs-it/cs-4521-steps-literal-bold-mac.png; js/data/content/cs-p2-45a.js:104 { h: '1.', m: 'Divide by the base; record the **remainder**…' }; js/core/content.js:404 esc(st.m)
fix: Move the prose to n (rendered through inline()) and drop the numeric h in those six leaves; optionally have validate_content.js flag markdown inside steps[].m and h matching /^\d+\.$/.
rootCause: Authoring misuse of the steps schema (m is the monospace working line, n the inline note).

title: ~30 CS flashcard decks ask the same fact twice ('Bandwidth?' + 'Define bandwidth.'), plus 11 cards duplicated across neighbouring leaves
detail: The depth rewrite added 'Define X.' / 'What does the MAR hold?' cards beside the original terse 'X?' / 'MAR holds…' cards without removing them, so the same definition is scheduled twice under FSRS. Confirmed by reading: 4.1.1.10 subroutine; 4.1.2.1 paradigm; 4.1.2.3 inheritance; 4.2.4.1 weighted graph and directed graph; 4.2.5.1 BST rule; 4.3.5.2 merge sort; 4.4.2.1 Mealy machine; 4.6.1.1 'Define software.' twice verbatim; 4.6.1.2 four types of system software; 4.6.5.1 'X + X̄·Y' and 'Simplify A + ¬A.B' (same identity, two notations); 4.7.3.1 MAR and MBR; 4.7.3.6 interrupt sources; 4.7.4.1 barcode reader; 4.7.4.2 optical disk; 4.9.1.1 'What is crosstalk?' twice verbatim; 4.9.1.2 bandwidth and latency; 4.9.2.1 physical and logical topology; 4.9.4.6 private ranges; 4.9.4.7 DHCP; 4.9.4.11 thin client (x2); 4.10.1 attribute; 4.10.2 primary key; 4.10.5 record locking and timestamp ordering. Across leaves: interface of a subroutine (4.1.1.10#15 / 4.1.1.11#2), data abstraction (4.2.1.1#7 / 4.4.1.3#20), floating vs fixed point advantages (4.5.4.4#17-18 / 4.5.4.7#0-1), four types of system software (4.6.1.2#0 / 4.6.1.3#7), three sources of interrupts (4.7.3.2#14 / 4.7.3.6#9), IPv6 and NAT (4.9.4.5#7 / 4.9.4.8#2), pitch opening (F204.6.1#6 / F206.5.1#5). The same Boolean deck also mixes overbar (X̄) and ¬ notation.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/content-cs-it/strict.txt (43 within-leaf pairs, confirmed by reading), audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/content-cs-it/cross.txt (11 cross-leaf pairs), audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/content-cs-it/dupes.txt (looser 800-line list); js/data/content/cs-p2-*.js flashcards arrays
fix: Keep the fuller 'Define X.' card and delete the terse twin in each pair; when deleting, add the original position as the third element to every later card (invariant 87) so schedules do not shift. Pick one Boolean notation per deck. Add a smoke66 near-duplicate check (token Jaccard on the question ≥ 0.9 within a leaf).
rootCause: Cards appended during the depth rewrite without de-duplicating against the original deck; no automated near-duplicate check.

title: IT F201 (the unit still to sit) is much thinner than CS: no worked answers, 3 exam items and 5–6 quiz questions per leaf
detail: Every F201 leaf has 0 worked examples, 0 figures, exactly 3 exam questions (no source), 5–6 quiz questions and 8–11 flashcards; notes run 493–1,281 words over 3–7 pages (F201.2.2 Data preparation 493 words and no table; F201.2.3 509; F201.5.1 517). CS leaves average ~1,900 words, 6–8 worked exam answers and 9–12 exam items. F201 is a 60-mark, 1 h 30 exam with six-mark and levels-of-response questions, yet there is no worked levels-of-response answer showing what a top-band 'Discuss' looks like, and 15 IT exam questions put '[6]' in the question text on top of the marks badge. The spec notes F201.2.6 lists 'Factor analysis' which the generated spec text does not (the spec row reads '□ Techniques To').
evidence: content-cs-it/metrics.txt (it F201.* rows: w0 fg0 ex3 q5-6); node scan: 15/150 IT exam q end with '[n]'; dump.json F201.2.3 spec ['□ Data mining','• Diagnostic Prescriptive □','□','□ Does','□']; audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/content-cs-it/it-f2013-p1-ipadl.png (a 60-word note page, half the iPad landscape screen empty)
fix: Add per F201 leaf: two worked exam answers (one 6-mark levels-of-response 'Discuss' with a band commentary), 6+ exam items across Describe/Explain/Discuss, 10 quiz questions, a scenario-based case per page; strip the '[n]' suffix from IT exam q text (marks already carry it).
rootCause: IT content was written to a lighter contract than smoke65/66 hold CS to; no IT depth smoke.

title: Bold containing an *italic* word renders literal ** in three IT F204 callouts
detail: KOS.content.inline's bold rule /\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/ cannot contain an asterisk, so '**health *and* home**' shows as '**health and home**' with the italic applied and literal asterisks. Seen in F204.1.1 'Sectors overlap' callout, F204.2.2 'How to write M6', F204.5.3 'A structure that scores' (this one also has a stray quote: '**(3) exactly what the solution does"**').
evidence: kos eval: KOS.content.inline('a **b *c* d** e') -> 'a **b c d** e'; js/core/content.js:109; js/data/content/it-f204.js:72, :544, :2189; render sweep content-cs-it/sweep-121.json
fix: Allow single-asterisk italics inside bold (process em inside strong: /\*\*((?:[^*]|\*(?!\*))+)\*\*/), and fix the misplaced quote at it-f204.js:2189.
rootCause: Inline markdown regex excludes * inside **…**.

title: Flashcards filed under the wrong leaf
detail: Cards that test a different topic than the leaf they sit in (confirmed by reading): 4.3.4.3 Binary tree search #13 asks which TRAVERSAL finds a range (4.3.2.1); 4.12.1.3 Function application #7 'head (tail (tail [4,7,1,9]))' is list processing (4.12.3.1); 4.5.6.1 Bit patterns #8 'How are instructions represented?' is the instruction set (4.7.3.3); 4.7.3.2 Fetch-Execute #14/#16 are interrupt cards (4.7.3.6); 4.9.4.3 IP address structure #9/#13 are IPv6/IPv4-exhaustion cards (4.9.4.5); 4.4.1.3 Kinds of abstraction #17 'Link to functional programming?' and #22 'Fraction built from…?' are synoptic asides as recall cards.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/content-cs-it/fit.txt (cards scored against other leaves' notes vocabulary, top hits confirmed by reading)
fix: Move each card to its home leaf (with a whole-key third element so its schedule follows, invariant 87) or delete it where the home leaf already has the fact.
rootCause: Cards authored as synoptic links ended up as plain recall cards in the wrong deck.

title: validate_content reports 9 errors in the CS merged leaves (cs-m-*) and 92 in IT: bare top-level paragraphs
detail: CLAUDE.md states `node tools/validate_content.js js/data/content/cs-*.js` reports no errors, but it reports 9 ERRORs, all bare string paragraphs in the merged-leaf files (4.4.1.9, 4.4.4.6, 4.5.1.1, 4.5.3.1, 4.5.4.1, 4.5.4.5, 4.5.6.1, 4.5.6.4 ×2: 'Steps an ADC performs (3 marks)…', 'Minimum file size = width × height × colour depth…'). These exam-technique paragraphs are exactly the content that should be a tip/formula callout. IT content has 92 bare-paragraph errors (F201.2.4 7, F201.2.3/2.5 5, F204.3.3 5 …), mostly the 'Characteristics: … When used: …' rows in F201 that render as loose prose between callouts.
evidence: node tools/validate_content.js js/data/content/cs-*.js → '45 file(s) checked — 9 error(s), 190 warning(s)'; it-*.js → '92 error(s), 120 warning(s)'; js/data/content/cs-m-errors.js, cs-m-bit-patterns.js
fix: Wrap each flagged paragraph in the fitting callout (tip for exam technique, formula for file-size rules); for IT, turn the 'Characteristics/When used' lines into a kv or table block per technique; add validate_content to the smoke gate so it cannot regress.
rootCause: The merged-leaf files were written after the validator pass, and the validator is not part of the smoke gate.

title: AQA mark-scheme shorthand (I., A., R., MAX, DPT) is used ~228 times with no explanation anywhere
detail: Worked steps' notes read 'I. an incorrect gate for B·C.', 'I. missing spaces; A. each digit on a new line', 'R. a column with more than one value', 'MAX 2 if not fully correct'. These are AQA examiner abbreviations (Ignore / Accept / Reject); a student meeting them on a phone reads 'I.' as a roman numeral or a first-person note. No legend exists in content.js, the worked card or Help.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/content-cs-it/cs-4641-p3-iphone.png (step 3 note 'I. an incorrect gate for B·C.'); grep '"[IAR]\. ' js/data/content/cs-*.js bank-cs-*.js → 228; js/data/content/cs-p1-411a.js, cs-p1-42c.js, cs-p1-43b.js
fix: Expand them at render in worked-step notes and mark-scheme bullets (I. → 'Ignore:', A. → 'Accept:', R. → 'Reject:') with a title on MAX/DPT, or add a one-line legend to the Exam questions tab and the worked card's footer.
rootCause: Mark points copied in AQA's house style without a reader-facing gloss.

title: Functional-programming code is tagged 'text' (no Haskell label or highlighting) and assembly shows the raw label 'asm'
detail: Every Haskell listing in 4.12.x (map/filter/fold definitions, partial application, composition, list processing — 11 blocks) is a {code} with lang 'text', so its head says 'text' and nothing is highlighted, while the C# twin beside it is coloured; the 4.7.3.5 assembly blocks print 'asm' because LANG_NAME has no entry for it.
evidence: dump scan of notes code blocks: 4.12.1.2/1.3/1.4/1.5/2.1/3.1 lang 'text', 4.7.3.5 lang 'asm'; js/core/content.js:70 LANG_NAME (no haskell/asm), :74 esc(LANG_NAME[lang] || lang)
fix: Tag those blocks lang 'haskell' and add 'haskell: "Haskell"', 'asm: "AQA assembly"' to LANG_NAME with a small keyword set in highlightCode (comments --, ::, ->).
rootCause: No highlighter/label for the two non-C# languages the AQA spec uses.

title: Stage path on touch devices: unit squares become 28x44 bars and capstone diamonds render as skewed slashes
detail: On iPad and iPhone (pointer: coarse) the desk hero's stage path (and every KOS.codeUI stage path) draws each unit square U1..U12 as a 28x44 tall rectangle and each capstone diamond as a 16x44 box rotated 45deg, which reads as a broken diagonal stroke rather than a diamond. Mac (fine pointer) is correct. Reproduce: #/subject/code at ipad/iphone.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-ipad.png, audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-iphone.png; eval at iphone: .k-cx-dia offsetWidth 16 x offsetHeight 44 with transform rotate(45deg); .k-cx-sq 28x44. css/base.css:115-119 (coarse min-block-size: var(--hit-coarse) on every button) vs css/views/code.css:132,137 (fixed inline-size/block-size), buttons made at js/core/codeui.js:556,567
rootCause: The global coarse-pointer rule raises min-block-size of every <button> to 44px (invariant 69) but the path's square/diamond buttons only set inline-size/block-size, so height grows and width does not; the diamond is then rotated.
fix: Give .k-cx-sq and .k-cx-dia min-block-size: 0 (they are visual marks; the diamond is tabindex -1) and put the 44px hit area on a transparent ::before or wrapper, or raise width with height for the squares (invariant 69: a round/square control must raise its width too).

title: iPhone desk: Daily 20 and Continue squeezed side by side; the Open-lesson button's label spills out of its pill
detail: At 402px the desk's side column (.k-subj-side) switches to a row, so Daily 20 and Continue are each ~180px wide. The Daily 20 body wraps to five lines, and the 'Open 1.1 Your first program' button is nowrap: its text (153px) overflows the 144px pill on both sides, so the label crosses the button border. Continue is a tall card with its content floating in the middle of ~200px of empty space, and its title wraps.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-iphone-d20.png (dpr 2), audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-iphone.png; eval iphone: [data-ui=code.daily20-lesson] 144x44, scrollWidth 153, white-space nowrap; .k-cx-d20 width 180. css/views/study.css:1074-1076 (side becomes a row of flex:1 1 0 cards), button at js/modules/code.js:221-223
rootCause: The phone/compact rule lays the side column as a row of two equal cards whatever their width; k-btn is nowrap with no max-inline-size or ellipsis, and the label names the lesson in full.
fix: Under 560px stack the two side cards (flex-direction: column) or fold Continue into the Daily 20 card when the Daily 20's job is 'Finish 1.1 first' (they point at the same lesson). Shorten the button to 'Open 1.1' or allow wrapping/ellipsis (.k-fit-btn).

title: Desk side column: a real Daily 20 task crushes the Continue card to 41px and clips its 'CONTINUE' label (Mac, iPad landscape)
detail: With a task in the Daily 20 (tier pill, title, three concept chips wrapping to two rows, the why line, Start), the Daily 20 card grows to 239px of the side column's fixed 292px (the hero's height). The Continue card gets 41px while its content needs 62px; overflow: hidden cuts the CONTINUE kicker in half under the Daily 20 card's border. Same at iPad landscape (d20 327 of 459, Continue 121, fits) and worse whenever the why line wraps to three lines. The concept chips (k-cx-cchips) wrap one per row on narrow cards, adding rows.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/code-space/desk-prog-mac.png (CONTINUE at y~396 cut); eval mac: .k-cx-d20 239px tall, [data-ui=study.continue] clientHeight 41 vs scrollHeight 62; side 292 = hero 292. css/views/study.css:50 (.k-subj-side > :first-child flex: 1 1 auto), :54 (contain: size), :55 (> * { min-block-size: 0; overflow: hidden }); js/modules/code.js:124, 228-234, 51-55
rootCause: The side column is size-contained to the hero's height and its children may shrink to zero with overflow hidden; the Daily 20 card (first child, flex 1 1 auto) takes what it needs, so the second card is what gives way and is clipped rather than the layout growing.
fix: Give the Continue card flex: 0 0 auto (never shrink below its content) and let the Daily 20 card scroll/clip instead, or drop size containment when the content is taller than the hero; render concept chips as one non-wrapping scroller or limit to two chips + '+1'.

title: Task Run can only feed ONE line of input: a correct answer to any multi-line task crashes with ArgumentNullException
detail: The task page's STDIN box is a single-line <input type=text>, prefilled with only the first line of the first example (split('\n')[0]). 158 of 258 tasks have multi-line example input. Pressing Run with the reference answer to 2.9 Guessing game (example input 42/50/30/42) gives 'Runtime exception ArgumentNullException line 5 Value cannot be null', because the second Console.ReadLine() returns null. A learner can never try their program on the example before Check, and the error points at correct code, which teaches the wrong lesson.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/code-space/task-run-multiline-mac.png; eval: set editor to KOS.code.task('2.9-guess').answer, click Run -> output 'ArgumentNullException line 5'; Object.values(KOS_CODE.TASKS) with multi-line examples[0].stdin = 158. js/modules/code.js:633-635 (input type text, split first line), :694 (stdin: stdin.value)
rootCause: Run's input was built as a one-line text field and deliberately truncates the example to its first line; an <input> cannot hold newlines.
fix: Use an auto-growing <textarea> (rows = example line count) prefilled with the whole first example stdin; keep Ctrl+Enter to run. Optionally a menu to load example N.

title: Subject analytics card stretches its eight tiles over the Retrieval-due list's height, leaving ~120px gaps between rows
detail: On the Code desk the analytics card (k-sa) is in a row with Retrieval due. With 4+ due skills the row is 412px tall and the grid (flex 1 1 0, grid-auto-rows 1fr, tiles justify-content center) spreads two rows of figures across it: Mastery/Lessons at y~560, Skills proven/Tasks passed at y~740, mostly empty dark card between. On iPad portrait (empty account) the 8 tiles stack 2 per row over ~450px, five of them showing only a dash. Conversely with nothing due the Retrieval-due card is a 250px card holding one sentence.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/code-space/desk-prog-mac.png, audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-ipad.png, audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/code-space/desk-empty-mac.png; eval mac: .k-sa 412px tall = retrieval-due 412px. css/views/study.css:77-78
rootCause: grid-auto-rows: 1fr with flex: 1 1 0 makes the tile rows absorb whatever height the neighbouring card imposes; tiles centre their content vertically.

title: Continue keeps pointing at 1.1 after the learner has worked through 22 lessons
detail: KOS.code.stats().current is the first core lesson whose status is not 'done'. Completed needs all four checks, and the fourth (a retrieval passed) cannot be earned until the card's first review comes due days later. So after reading every page, running every listing and passing every task in lessons 1.1-3.5 (and starting 3.6), the desk's Continue card still says '1.1 Your first program' at 75%, and the hero's current unit ring stays on U1. The learner's real place (3.6) is nowhere on the desk.
evidence: eval after marking pages/listings/tasks for 22 lessons: stats().current.ref = '1.1', evidence('1.1').checks = [true,true,true,false]; audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/code-space/desk-prog-mac.png (Continue 1.1). js/core/code.js:870 (current = first not done), js/modules/code.js:250-262
rootCause: 'Where to continue' is derived from completion (which includes a time-gated retrieval) instead of coverage (KOS.code.studied) or the last lesson touched.
fix: Continue at the first lesson not yet studied (KOS.code.studied false), or the most recently touched unfinished lesson; leave pending retrievals to the Retrieval card.

title: Retrieval's 'Next reviews will ask…' dates come from a hard-coded SM-2 formula and contradict the real FSRS schedule
detail: Under a card the page projects its next three reviews as 'in 3 days / in 11 days / in 31 days', computed with ivl*2.5 (SM-2). Answering the card first try (graded Easy by FSRS) shows 'Proven · Easy · next in 8 days' directly above a table still saying 'in 3 days'. Since 20 October every card is scheduled by KOS.fsrs (invariant 111); the projection is invented and never matches. The page subtitle also keeps '6 due today' after the tab count dropped to 5.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/code-space/retrieval-after-check-mac.png (next in 8 days vs table in 3 days); js/modules/code.js:1013-1020 (var ivl = Math.max(3, row.ivl||2), ef = 2.5 … ivl*ef)
rootCause: The projection predates the FSRS switch and was not moved to KOS.fsrs; it is not redrawn after a rating.
fix: Project with KOS.fsrs (Good each time from the card's current s/d with KOS.srs.weights() and the retention) or drop the dates and keep only the variation list; redraw after finish().

title: Choosing 'Media' in the Japanese spine locks the device out of every Japanese lesson: each lesson page throws 'codeSpine.stageHead is not a function' and bounces to Home, and the switch back is on the page that no longer opens
detail: The Japanese spine has a Core | Media segment (state.ui.japanese.spine, per device, saved). In Media mode KOS.jaTopic.spine() returns { tracks: true } with no stageHead. hub.js renderTree then calls codeSpine.stageHead(sec.stage) for the first section (it only checks that codeSpine is truthy), which throws; KOS.views.ref aborts, the router shows the toast 'A page could not be opened.' and replaces the route with #/home. Because the choice is saved, every later attempt to open ANY Japanese lesson — the desk's Continue, the path squares, the Practice links, search, Back — fails the same way, and the only control that resets the mode is the Core button inside that spine. Code: js/modules/jatopic.js:36-40 (media branch returns {tracks:true} only); js/modules/hub.js:491-495 (stageHead called whenever codeSpine is truthy).

Add a smoke test that opens a ja lesson with ui.japanese.spine = 'media'. Until the media release, consider hiding the Media segment.
rootCause: Spine contract (stageHead) not honoured by the Media branch; caller does not guard

title: 'Held in reviews' (4th lesson check) is never written to the progress record by reviews, so the inspector shows 3/4 · 75% while the stored status, spine and unit counts stay behind
detail: KOS.ja.syncChecks is called only from markPage, markHeard and finishLesson (js/core/ja.js:106,112,241) — never from record()/finishSession() or at boot. The 4th check (every item's R/L facet reps ≥ 2 and s ≥ 7) can only become true later, through review sessions, so it is never synced unless the learner happens to open an unread page or play an unheard line of that lesson afterwards. The inspector computes evidence live and shows the check ticked and '3 of 4 checks 75%', while the shared progress record (which drives the status select 'Started', the spine's 'F1 0 / 6', 'Kana to native media 0 / 28 completed', the subject's mastery in Home/Reports/Goals and the auto Completed status) keeps check[3] = false. A lesson can therefore never reach Completed through reviews.
evidence: eval: after reading all 8 pages of 1.1, finishLesson, and holding every item's R facet (reps 3, s 30): KOS.ja.evidence('1.1').checks = [true,false,true,true] but KOS.store.peekProgress('ja','1.1').check = [true,false,true,false] (also after rendering the topic page). Screenshot /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-1.1-heldmismatch-mac.png: inspector ticks 'Held in reviews 14 of 14 items held' and '3 of 4 checks 75%' beside status 'Started', spine 'F1 First conversations 0 / 6'.
fix: After KOS.ja.record()/finishSession(), call syncChecks for every lesson whose items were reviewed (map item → lesson), and run a one-pass syncChecks over all started lessons at boot (as Code's syncChecks is run), so the stored checks always equal evidence().
rootCause: Evidence that changes through the scheduler has no write path into the progress record

title: Leaving a Japanese session by navigation (rail, tab bar, Back, iPad edge swipe, reload) logs nothing: answers are rescheduled but the session's XP and the day's study activity are lost
detail: Each answer is written to the facet at once (KOS.ja.record), but the ONE ledger entry (finishSession → KOS.sessions.log) is written only by end(): reaching the last card or confirming the ✕ dialog. Any other exit — the rail, the phone tab bar, browser Back, the iPad's back swipe, closing the Home Screen app — discards results[]. The facets move (the work is 'done' and will not be asked again today) but no XP is paid, the session never counts toward the study streak or the day's activity, and Reports/Goals/Badges that read the ledger never see it. The ✕ dialog's promise ('What you have answered is kept and scheduled') is only half kept elsewhere.
evidence: eval slot 10: two kana R facets due; open #/japanese/session/reviews, answer さ correctly (facet reps 0 → 1), KOS.show('home') → new ledger entries 0, governor XP +0. js/modules/jarun.js:400-406 (leave only on ✕), :431-447 end(); no hashchange/pagehide/KOS.show hook in run().
fix: Log the session on teardown: register a one-shot on the next KOS.show / router leave and on pagehide (as Focus banks on page hide, invariant 4c) that calls end(true) when results.length && !done; or log incrementally (one entry per session id, updated) so nothing depends on the exit path.
devices: all (most likely on iPad/iPhone via the back swipe and tab bar)
rootCause: Ledger write tied to an explicit end event; navigation tears the view down silently

detail: On iPad (portrait and landscape) and iPhone: (1) the stage path's checkpoint buttons (data-ui ja.path-checkpoint) are 21x44 — a thin target between unit squares, and they are the only way to open a checkpoint from the desk's path; (2) Mind Journal's kind filter chips (.k-mind-kindpick: All, Insight, Quote, Question, Position, Reflection) are 32px tall on touch; (3) Japanese settings' Daily minutes range input is 129x16.
