title: Japanese learn session asks Listening first and buries every Reading facet (sibling tie-break sorts 'L' before 'R')
detail: Start lesson 1.1 on an empty account: KOS.ja.due() returns j:本|R and then only the |L facet of every word and pattern (w:これ|L, g:ka|L, …); every |R facet is buried as a sibling. jarun.run then sorts 'Reading before Listening', but the R facets were already removed, so a brand-new word is met and immediately asked by ear (listen-pick: hear it, pick the meaning) with no reading check at all on day one. The code's stated intent (jarun.js:369 'the lesson's own facets, Reading first') is not what happens.
evidence: eval slot 10 after KOS.ja.startLesson('1.1'): due = [j:本|R, g:ka|L, g:kosoa|L, g:wa-desu|L, w:あれ|L, w:かさ|L, w:これ|L, …] (no word |R). Root: js/core/jasrs.js:105-107 sort tie-break (a.k < b.k) puts '|L' before '|R' when over and recall are equal (new facets: 0, 0), then :110-111 keeps only the first facet of each item.
fix: In queue(), break ties by skill order (R, L, W, S, H) before the key string, or in jarun.run for a learn session take the lesson's facets from KOS.ja.peek().facets directly rather than the sibling-buried due() list.
rootCause: Alphabetical key tie-break in the sibling-burying queue

title: Sibling rule broken within a day: once one facet of an item is answered, its buried sibling becomes due the same day
detail: Invariant 113: 'Two facets of one item never share a day unless both are over two days overdue.' queue() only buries a sibling among facets that are due at the same moment; it keeps no memory of what was reviewed today. After answering w:これ|L (due moves to +10 days), w:これ|R is the item's only due facet, so the next session the same day (or 'Reviews' from the desk straight after the lesson) asks it.
evidence: eval: KOS.ja.record('w:これ|L', {verdict:'correct',ms:2000}) then KOS.ja.due().indexOf('w:これ|R') >= 0 → true (same day 2026-11-05). js/core/jasrs.js:101-114 filters only by f.due <= today; no check of a sibling's f.last === today.
fix: In queue(), skip a facet whose sibling has last === today (unless both are >2 days overdue), or push the buried sibling's due to tomorrow when its sibling is reviewed in record().
rootCause: Burying is computed over the current due set only, with no 'reviewed today' memory

title: One fast correct answer unlocks the Writing facet at once: 'R holds a week' is read as first-review stability ≥ 7 days, which a single Easy gives (s 8.3)
detail: Invariant 113: 'W (and S for a word) only once R holds a week.' facetsFor() treats held as r.reps && r.s >= HOLD (7). A first-ever answer inside the 4 s target grades Easy (gradeOf), and FSRS-6's initial Easy stability is 8.2956 days, so the very first correct reading of a production word or pattern unlocks W the same minute. The same single answer schedules the word 10 days out. Thin evidence (one multiple-choice tap or one typed answer) is treated as a held item.
evidence: eval after startLesson('1.1'): KOS.ja.record('w:これ|R',{verdict:'correct',hints:0,ms:2000}).unlocked = ['w:これ|W']; KOS.ja.record('g:ka|R',{…ms:3000}).unlocked = ['g:ka|W']; facet after one answer {s: 8.2956, ivl: 10}. js/core/jasrs.js:62 held = r.reps && r.s >= HOLD; js/core/jasrs.js:45 a correct answer within target → 4 (Easy) regardless of tries; js/core/ja.js:35 TARGET R 4000 ms.
fix: Define 'holds a week' as evidence over time: reps >= 2 and a successful review at least 7 days after firstAt (or last - firstAt >= 7 with the last grade >= Good). Also cap a first-ever answer at Good, so a brand-new item is not pushed 10 days out by one tap.
rootCause: Stability used as a proxy for elapsed holding time

title: 'Passed the practice' ticks and the lesson pays 15 XP · 2 gold · +3 HP even when every answer in the learn session is wrong
detail: A learn session that reaches the end calls KOS.ja.finishLesson whenever results.length > 0 (jarun.js end()), with no pass condition. finishLesson sets doneAt (which IS the 'Passed the practice' check, evidence() checks[2] = !!rec.doneAt) and pays LESSON_PAY on the first finish. Contradictory evidence test: 17 answers all wrong, slow (9 s) → fs {passed: 0, paid: 0} but fl {paid: true, pay {xp 15, gold 2, hp 3}}, the check reads 'Passed the practice · passed', the unit counts the lesson as done (unitState F1 done 1/6) and nextLesson() moves on. The inspector label promises a pass that never happened.
evidence: eval slot 10: startLesson('1.2'), record every due lesson facet {verdict:'wrong', ms:9000}, finishSession, finishLesson → {paid:true, pay:{xp:15,gold:2,hp:3}}, evidence('1.2').checks = [false,false,true,false], governor xp 0 → 15. Code: js/modules/jarun.js:435 'if (lessonId && !early && results.length) paidLesson = KOS.ja.finishLesson(lessonId)'; js/core/ja.js:234-245 (no pass test); js/core/ja.js:136 checks[2] = !!rec.doneAt.
fix: Require a pass to finish: e.g. at least 60–70% of the lesson's graded answers Hard or better (or each item answered right at least once, re-asking the misses at the end of the session as Code/flashcards do). Otherwise end with 'Not passed yet — try the misses again', no pay, no doneAt. Rename the check if it only means 'finished the practice'.
rootCause: Lesson completion is 'reached the end of the session', not 'passed'

title: A Japanese leech (8 lapses) leaves the schedule for good: Rework rows are inert text with no way to relearn or put the facet back, and a leech looks the same as a 5-lapse item
detail: jasrs.queue drops every facet with lapses ≥ 8 (invariant 113 'sets a facet aside'). Nothing ever un-sets it: there is no unleech in KOS.ja/jaSrs, and the Rework card (desk and Skill map) renders each row as a plain div — no button, link or 'Back in the schedule' — even though its footnote promises 'Rework teaches the item again from its own lesson'. Flashcards' equivalent (invariant 111b) offers the topic's notes and 'Back in the schedule'. The rows also do not say which items are set aside: ねこ at 8× (out of the queue) and ペン at 5× (still due) look identical.
evidence: eval: w:ねこ|L lapses 8 → KOS.ja.due() excludes it, w:ペン|L lapses 5 → included; KOS.ja.rework() lists both. DOM: [data-ui~='ja.rework-row'] → DIV with 0 buttons/links. Screenshot /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-skills-rework-mac.png. Code: js/modules/japanese.js:238-247 (rows), :498 (the promise); js/core/jasrs.js:96,102 (leech filter); no unleech anywhere (grep).
fix: Make each Rework row a button that opens the item's lesson at its Quick reference (or a mini learn session for that item), mark set-aside facets ('Set aside · 8 lapses'), and add KOS.ja.unleech(key) (lapses back to a base, as KOS.srs.unleech's leechBase) behind 'Back in the schedule'.
rootCause: Rework was drawn as a report, the relearn path was never built

title: Three promises the Japanese space cannot keep: 'Input this week' never fills (addInput has no caller), the Speaking switch changes nothing, and Licences say JMdict/KANJIDIC2/Tatoeba 'arrive with Stage 1' though Stage 1 shipped without them
detail: (1) The desk's 'Input this week' card says 'Watching and reading in Japanese counts here, through Focus', but KOS.ja.addInput is defined and exported and called nowhere (no Focus path, no reader), so the card is permanently empty. (2) Settings › Speech is a working switch with an opt-in dialog about sending audio to Google, but KOS.ja.opts() hard-codes speech:false (js/core/ja.js:87-89 'false until the Speech release') and no S exercise exists, so turning it on has no effect beyond un-dimming the S column on the desk. (3) Licences & credits list JMdict, KANJIDIC2 and Tatoeba with 'Arrives with Stage 1' — Stage 1 units F1 and F2 are released and use authored items, none from those sources.
evidence: grep: 'addInput(' only at js/core/ja.js:291 (definition) and the export; js/modules/japanese.js:283-285 (empty-state promise), :656-657 (switch), :665 'row("Speech", …)', :674-676 (licence rows). js/core/ja.js:87-89 speech:false. No JMdict/Tatoeba reference in js/data/ja*.js or js/data/content/ja-*.js.
fix: Hide the Input card (or wire a 'Japanese immersion' Focus choice that calls addInput) until it can be filled; hide or disable the Speech switch with 'arrives with the Speech release'; reword the licence rows to 'Arrives with the reader/dictionary' or drop them until used.
rootCause: Pages drawn for the full plan before their features shipped

title: Kana Writing reviews show the answer: the model glyph sits beside the pad on every review, so 'Write it' is a copying exercise graded as recall
detail: In a review session, a kana Writing facet (k:あ|W, reps > 0) draws the pad AND the model card ('あ · a · 3 strokes · copy the model') unconditionally. The learner can trace the visible model and the stroke check grades it like recall (correct inside 12 s → Easy, a 2–4× longer interval). Only the stroke animation is gated on the first attempt (jarun.js:168). Writing from memory is the whole point of the W facet once it has been met.
evidence: Screenshot /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-sessk2-ipad.png (Reviews 2/4, Writing · A · write it, model あ shown beside the pad). js/modules/jarun.js:142-146 builds the model, :167 appends it always; :148 'first' only controls the animation.
fix: Show the model only on the first meeting (reps 0) and as a 'Show the model' hint that counts as a hint (grade Hard) afterwards; prompt with the romaji reading only ('Write: a').
rootCause: The learn-time layout is reused for reviews

title: Grades are more lenient than the rules say: a retry after 'near' can still grade Easy, and a stroke check 'accepted' (a stroke 'a little off', even ね drawn as two straight lines) is upgraded to 'correct'
detail: (1) gradeOf gives Easy for any 'correct' within the target time (jasrs.js:45-46); the comment and plan say 'a first try inside the target', but jarun.finish only passes hints and ms — tries is never sent — so a near-miss followed by Retry and a quick correct answer is Easy. (2) jarun's kana-write maps the stroke validator's 'accepted' to 'correct' (jarun.js:150), dropping both the note and the Good cap that 'accepted' carries everywhere else (gradeOf: accepted → Good). The stroke tolerance is wide: a ね made of two straight lines from each reference stroke's start to its end returns 'accepted'; every reference shifted 11/109 units returns 'accepted' (あ, ぬ, め, ね, さ); a shape at 60% size returns 'correct'. With the mapping each of these can grade Easy.
evidence: eval slot 10: KOS.jaStroke.check('ね', straight lines start→end of each KanjiVG stroke).verdict = 'accepted'; shift +11 → 'accepted' for あぬめねさ ('near' for き); scaled 0.6 → 'correct' (あぬめね). Code: js/modules/jarun.js:104-106 (finish passes hints, ms only), :150 ('accepted' → 'correct'); js/core/jasrs.js:40-47; js/core/jastroke.js:66 OK=13 / OFF=24 in a 109 box.
fix: Pass tries into the result and grade Easy only when tries === 1; keep the stroke verdict 'accepted' (Good, show its note); consider tightening OFF for long curved strokes (e.g. compare curvature/turning angle, not only mean point distance).
rootCause: Result object lacks tries; verdict upgrade in the runner

title: '▶ Practise again' on a finished lesson opens an empty session ('Nothing due right now') and sends you to the desk, not back to the lesson
detail: A finished lesson's Practice tab offers '▶ Practise again' (jatopic.js:269). It opens #/japanese/session/learn-<id>, whose list is KOS.ja.due() filtered to the lesson's items (jarun.js:364-375) — so when none of them is due today (the normal case once a lesson is done) the runner shows a 460px card with 'Nothing due right now' and a single 'Back to the desk' button, which leaves the lesson the learner came from. The button promises practice that cannot happen; there is no cram/extra-practice mode (reviews are not moved by it, so one is easy to add).
evidence: eval: lesson 1.1 done, all its facets due 2026-12-30 → #/japanese/session/learn-1.1 → 'Nothing due right now · Back to the desk'. Screenshot /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-practise-again-empty-mac.png.
fix: For a finished lesson run an unscheduled practice over its items (self-contained, record nothing or record as practice that moves no facet), or hide 'Practise again' when nothing of the lesson is due and say when its items come back. 'Back to the desk' should return to the lesson when the session was opened from it.
rootCause: The learn session reuses the due queue, which is empty after the first finish

title: Media path projects absurd ranges from thin evidence ('Graded reader Level 1 · 2032 – 2084', 'A light novel · 2180 – 3559') once two weeks pass with a single word met
detail: timeline() stops calibrating as soon as the first R facet is 14+ days old and the mean weekly rate is above 0. With one word met 10 days ago and one kana 20 days ago: perWeek {lo 0, mid 1, hi 1}; lo is floored at 0.1 words/week, so 'to' = (need − have)/0.1 × 7 days → every stone gets a range spanning decades to centuries, shown on the path, the stone detail and All stones. Related on the same page: the kana stone shows 'Calibrating' in All stones forever (it never gets a date because the rate is in words; js/modules/japanese.js:548 prints 'Calibrating' whenever m.from is null), 'about 1 new words a week' (plural), the kana requirement says 'Hiragana stable 1 / 46' counting kana held 7 days (HOLD) while the Skill map's 'stable' means 21 days (STABLE), and the 'Next stone' card is about twice as tall as its content beside the levers card.
evidence: eval fixture: facets {k:あ|R firstAt −20d, w:これ|R firstAt −10d} → KOS.ja.timeline() {calibrating:false, perWeek:{lo:0,mid:1,hi:1}, Graded reader 2032-07-29 → 2084-02-24, Yotsuba 2049 → 2256}. Screenshot /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-path-thin-mac.png. Code: js/core/ja.js:376-388 (calibrating = span < 14 || mean <= 0; lo = max(0.1, mean − sd)); js/modules/japanese.js:524,548 (subhead, 'Calibrating' fallback).
fix: Stay calibrating until there is a real rate (e.g. ≥ 2 weeks with words AND ≥ 20 words met), cap projections (e.g. beyond 3 years say 'more than 3 years at this pace'), give the kana stone its own rate (basic kana held per week) or a 'kana first' label instead of 'Calibrating', pluralise, and use one 'stable' threshold wording.
rootCause: No minimum-evidence gate besides elapsed time; a floor of 0.1/week makes the upper bound explode

title: Checkpoints are easier than '80% in every skill' suggests: the Hiragana checkpoint's 6 Listening questions are 3 two-choice items each asked twice identically, and the Writing section shows the model kana to copy
detail: checkpointRun builds cp-H's Listening section as sounds.concat(sounds).slice(0,6) — the unit's three minimal-pair items (s:voicing, s:sokuon, s:long) twice. exercise() seeds the pair and target from hash(key + today), so the repeat is the very same pair with the same answer, asked after the verdict revealed it; each is a 2-option guess. The Writing section mounts the same kana-write exercise as reviews, which always shows the model glyph beside the pad ('copy the model'), so the writing score measures tracing. The question selection is also fixed for the whole day (seed = the date), so a retake the same day repeats the same paper.
evidence: js/modules/japanese.js:593 (sounds.concat(sounds)), :589-590 (pick seeded by the day); js/modules/jarun.js:31-34 (minimal pair seeded by key + today), :142-146/167 (model always shown). eval: cp-H unit has exactly 3 sound items ['s:voicing','s:sokuon','s:long'].
fix: Draw 6 distinct pairs across the three items' pair lists (each item has several pairs) with a per-question seed; hide the model in checkpoint Writing; seed the selection per attempt (Date.now()) rather than per day.
rootCause: Too few listening items padded by duplication; one exercise renderer for learn, review and test

title: Japanese is missing from Goals and Reports: no goal type measures it and Reports has no Japanese facts, unlike Code (f.code, code-tasks/retrievals) and Creatives (f.creatives, cr-*)
detail: The Goals registry has study, productivity, money, code, creatives and governor types but nothing that reads KOS.ja (no 'Japanese review sessions', 'lessons finished', 'kana held', 'words stable'); 'Review flashcards' counts only flashcards/due-review entries, so Japanese facet reviews never count even with the subject set to Japanese. Reports' compute() builds f.code (programming(), report.js:614) and f.creatives (:645) from their ledger entries, but there is no counterpart for type 'ja' entries (sessions with n/passed/skills, lessons, checkpoints): a week of Japanese reviews appears at most as an untimed study session, never as reviews, lessons or checkpoints. The only joins are the routine auto-track (routines.js:646) and badges. 'KurenaiOS should be one connected personal OS' — the space is an island for planning and review.
evidence: grep register({ id in js/core/goals.js → custom-manual, study-hours, cards-reviewed, recall-rate, topics-green, focus-*, todos-done, plan-ticked, study-paper-score, study-finish-unit, habit-streak, no-overdue, carryovers-cleared, money-*, code-tasks, code-retrievals, code-capstone, cr-studies, cr-drill-days, cr-words, gov-streak, gov-level (none for ja); js/core/goals.js:557-562 (cards-reviewed: flashcards only); js/core/report.js:614,645 (code/creatives facts), no 'ja' filter anywhere in report.js.
fix: Register ja goal types (ja-reviews: passed facets or sessions; ja-lessons; ja-kana-held; ja-words-stable) reading KOS.ja/the ledger, and add f.ja (sessions, facets passed by skill, lessons finished, checkpoints) to Reports with a card, totals only in the words' payload, as Code's.
rootCause: Japanese shipped its platform before the cross-domain joins its sibling spaces got

title: Kana page: switching Mixed / Read / Write mid-set (or leaving without 'End set') throws the set's answers away unlogged
detail: The kana drill keeps its answers in a local results[] and logs them only from 'End set' (endSet → finishSession). The Mixed/Read/Write segment calls KOS.rerender() directly, which rebuilds the page with an empty results[]; navigation does the same. The facets were already moved by record(), so the kana is not asked again today, but no ledger entry is written: no XP, no day activity, no 'Japanese review session' for an auto-tracked habit (routines.js:646). Same root cause as the session runner's navigation loss.
evidence: eval slot 10 on #/japanese/kana after startLesson('H1'): answer あ correctly → set '1 of 10', facet k:あ|R reps 1 (due +10 d); click 'Read' → '0 of 10', new ledger entries 0. js/modules/japanese.js:370-371 (segment → KOS.rerender), :375-380 (endSet the only logger).
fix: Log the pending results before the mode switch rerenders (call endSet first, or keep results in per-device UI state), and on navigation/pagehide as for the session runner.
rootCause: Session results held only in closure state across a rerender

title: iPhone Kana chart hides the や, ら, わ and ん columns off the left edge with no cue: an undeclared overflow scroller
detail: At 402 px the chart's .k-ja-chart-cols (flex row-reverse, overflow-x auto) is 326 px for 524 px of columns, so the four leftmost columns (ya, ra, wa, n — including the dashes the caption explains) start at x −160 and are only reachable by an unseen horizontal swipe (scrollbars are hidden on iOS); there is no arrow, fade or 'scroll' hint, and it is not a KOS.ui.scroller (invariant 50: horizontal overflow must be declared). The caption under it ('A dash is a sound modern Japanese doesn't use (yi, ye, wu…)') refers to columns the learner cannot see.
evidence: Screenshot /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-kana-iphone.png (chart shows ま…あ only). eval (iphone): .k-ja-chart-cols scrollWidth 524 / clientWidth 326, ん column left −160, scrollLeft can go to −198, not inside .k-scroller. css/views/japanese.css:225.
fix: Wrap the columns in KOS.ui.scroller (arrows + edge fade, starting at the あ end), or under 560 px drop the gap and shrink cells to fit 11 columns (11 × 30 px), or split the chart into two rows of columns.

title: Study-space heroes are four different heights: the Japanese desk hero is 339 px on the Mac against Code's 292 and Mind's 296 (iPad 507 vs 459/482, iPhone 458 vs 379/402/309)
detail: All four study spaces use the same .k-subj-hero at the same width (900 px mac, 716 iPad, 370 iPhone) but its height follows its content: Japanese has four skill rows (Reading, Listening, Writing, Speaking) on the right and the six-stage path underneath, so it is 47 px taller than Code on the Mac and 79 px taller on the iPhone. Switching between the space pills (Code · Japanese · Mind · Creatives) makes the whole page below jump. The user's standing rule names exactly this ('study-space heroes of different sizes').
evidence: eval (seeded slot, after this audit's fixtures) .k-subj-hero height: mac {code 292, ja 339, mind 296, creatives 341}; ipad {459, 507, 482, 509}; iphone {379, 458, 402, 309}. Screenshot /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-desk-dawn-mac.png.
fix: Give the hero one shared block size per breakpoint (tokens), with the right column's rows compressed (Japanese: 4 thinner skill rows, Speaking dimmed in one line) and the stage path inside the same budget; or set the hero to a fixed aspect so art and content line up across spaces.
rootCause: Content-sized hero with per-space content of different heights

title: Stage-path checkpoint circles render as 21×44 ovals on iPad and iPhone
detail: On touch devices the desk's and Checkpoints page's stage-path checkpoint stops (合 between the unit squares) get the coarse-pointer 44 px height but keep their ~21 px width with border-radius 50%, so each draws as a tall dark ellipse between the H / K / F1 / F2 squares — exactly the '28×44 oval' invariant 69 forbids ('a round control must raise its width too'). (The undersized touch target of the same element is the earlier entry in this file; this is the visual.)
evidence: Screenshot /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-desk-empty-iphone.png (stage row: ovals between H, K, F1, F2). eval (iphone): [data-ui~='ja.path-checkpoint'] 21×44, border-radius 50%, background oklch(0.2 0.009 265).
fix: Draw the circle as an inner element of fixed size (e.g. 22 px) centred in a 44×44 transparent hit box, or set aspect-ratio: 1 with min-inline-size = min-block-size under (pointer: coarse) and rebalance the path columns.
rootCause: Global coarse-pointer min-height applied to a round control without a matching width

title: The Assistant and the day model know nothing about Japanese: no ja_* read tool, and KOS.today/the reviews never mention Japanese reviews due
detail: Invariant 71a: 'The Assistant has tools for every domain'. aitools.js defines code_overview/code_lesson/code_skills, mind_overview/mind_concept, creatives_overview/creatives_portfolio, but zero tools mention Japanese (grep count 0), so 'How is my Japanese going?' or 'What should I review today?' cannot be answered from data. KOS.today.build (the source for Home's three, the Morning/Evening reviews and the Assistant's day, invariant 149) reads no KOS.ja either, so a day with 40 Japanese facets due never surfaces outside the Japanese desk; only the evening review counts finished ja lessons (dayreview.js:355).
evidence: grep -c '"ja\|japanese\|Japanese' js/core/aitools.js → 0; def('creatives_overview') at js/core/aitools.js:898 as the pattern; js/core/today.js has no KOS.ja reference; js/core/dayreview.js:355.
fix: Add read tools ja_overview (stats, due by skill, today's plan, next lesson, timeline range) and ja_lesson (evidence, items held), and give KOS.today a 'Japanese reviews due / next lesson' entry when started().
rootCause: Cross-domain joins not built for the Japanese release

title: A passed checkpoint shows 'Passed · paid once' beside '10% ✗ Not yet' in every skill after a weaker retake — the last attempt's scores overwrite the passing ones
detail: recordCheckpoint stores rec.scores = the latest attempt's scores on every take, while passAt is kept. After passing (R 0.8 W 0.8 L 0.83) and retaking badly (0.1 each), the Checkpoints card draws the 合 seal and 'Passed on Thu 5 Nov · ◆ paid once' above three red '10% ✗ Not yet' rows — a self-contradicting card. The best (passing) attempt is lost.
evidence: eval: recordCheckpoint('cp-H', {R:.8,W:.8,L:5/6}) → pass, paid; recordCheckpoint('cp-H', {R:.1,W:.1,L:.1}) → rec {scores 0.1×3, passAt set}. Screenshot /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-cps2-mac.png. js/core/ja.js:254 rec.scores = sc unconditionally.
fix: Keep best (or the passing) scores separately from the last attempt (rec.best, rec.last) and show 'Passed' with the passing scores, the last attempt as a secondary line.

title: Mind lesson inspector has no status selector, confidence (RAG) or progress bar, unlike every other study space
detail: On a Code, Japanese or Creatives lesson the inspector carries the shared status row (Not started · Started · Paused · Completed select), the R/A/G confidence picker and a percent bar (invariant 107: the status 'may still be set by hand, as in a subject'). A Mind lesson's inspector shows only 'STATUS 0 of 4 checks' and the four read-only checks: no way to mark a lesson Paused or set confidence, and no percentage, although the desk and spine count Mind lessons by that same shared status.
evidence: js/modules/mindtopic.js:361-386 ctx.status builds only the head and checkgrid; compare js/modules/jatopic.js:295-318, js/modules/crtopic.js:220-243, js/modules/codetopic.js:160-210 (status select + KOS.rag.picker). Screenshots /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/ja-mind/e-mind-F1.1-mac.png vs /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/ja-mind/e-ja-1.1-mac.png
fix: Reuse the same status/RAG block (ideally hoist it into one shared helper used by all four topic modules, since it is copy-pasted three times) and add it to ctx.status in mindtopic.js.
rootCause: Each study space's topic module re-implements the inspector status block; Mind's copy omitted the row

title: Japanese lesson inspector reads '0 of 1 sessions'
detail: On a Japanese Stage 1 lesson (e.g. #/ref/ja/1.1) the inspector's check 'Passed the practice' has the sub-line '0 of 1 sessions' — a hard-coded string with the wrong plural.
evidence: js/modules/jatopic.js:297 ev.practised ? "passed" : "0 of 1 sessions"; screenshot /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/ja-mind/e-ja-1.1-mac.png (inspector, third check)
fix: 'not yet' (or '0 of 1 session'); the count is always one, so say 'one session' / 'not passed yet'.

title: Multiple-choice exercises never show which option was right after a wrong pick
detail: In listen-pick, particle-pick, read-meaning and listen-meaning, picks() disables every option and sets each one's state from the PICKED option (closure variable opt) instead of its own option, then marks the picked one. After a wrong pick only the chosen button turns red; the correct option stays neutral (data-state null). The verdict box below does print the answer, but the learner has to map it back to the options.
evidence: Screenshot /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-sess2-mac.png; DOM after picking 'I'm a student.': [{"Nice to meet you, I'm Yōta.", state null}, {"I'm a student.", state 'wrong'}, {"It's a Japanese book.", state null}]. js/modules/jarun.js:211-214 (forEach uses opt, not the button's own option).
fix: Store each option on its button (b._opt) and in the forEach set KOS.ui.state(b, 'right', b._opt === ok); keep 'wrong' on the picked button only.

title: Session runner leaks internal exercise-family codes ('A · read it', 'C · read and understand', 'D · listen and pick') into the skill line
detail: The line above each exercise reads 'Reading  C · read and understand', 'Writing  A · write it'. The A–E letters are the plan's exercise families (docs/japanese-plan.md) and mean nothing to the learner.
evidence: Screenshots /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-sess1-mac.png, q-sessk2-ipad.png. js/modules/jarun.js:29-49 family strings.
fix: Drop the letter prefix: 'Reading · read and understand'.

title: 'Type instead' on a kana Writing review passes the Writing facet for typing its romaji (e.g. 'a' for あ)
detail: 'Type instead' swaps the stroke pad for the kana-READ exercise (type the reading of the glyph that is shown) but keeps the W facet key, then grades it Hard — a pass that pays +1 XP and advances the Writing schedule. Typing 'a' while あ is on screen shows nothing about writing it.
evidence: eval on #/japanese/session/reviews (ipad): click [data-ui~='ja.type-instead'], type 'a', Check → 'Grade, from your answer · Hard · next tomorrow'; facet k:あ|W reps 1, s 1.29. js/modules/jarun.js:159-165.
fix: Make 'Type instead' an IME/kana-keyboard production (type あ in kana from the romaji prompt, glyph hidden), or record it self-marked (moves nothing) and say so.

title: Minimal-pair options render the kana in the UI font at 15px with the beat count glued on ('ケキ2 beats')
detail: The minimal-pair option group has no data-state='ja', so css/views/japanese.css:356 (the English-options rule) overrides the 22px Japanese font of .k-ja-opt; the kana and its <small> beat count are inline with 0px gap, reading 'ケキ2 beats' / 'ケーキ3 beats', left-aligned, while every other Japanese option is centred-large Japanese type.
evidence: Screenshot /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/ja-mind/q-sessk3-ipad.png; measured gap between span and small = 0, .k-ja-opt display block. js/modules/jarun.js:182-189 (no data-state on the group); css/views/japanese.css:154,356.
fix: Give the minimal-pair group data-state='ja' and lay the option out as a column (word large, '2 beats' small muted beneath), or a flex with a gap.

title: Three Japanese badges can never be earned (Voice, Immersion, Sentence miner) yet are registered as live badges, and Japanese reviews never re-measure the Badge Wall
detail: Invariant 161: 'a badge the app has no evidence for is not registered'. 'Voice' counts S facets (never created: KOS.ja.opts speech:false), 'Immersion' counts state.japanese.input minutes (addInput has no caller) and 'Sentence miner' counts state.japanese.mined (KOS.ja.mine has no caller) — all three sit on the Wall at 0 with tier targets (50/10 h/10 lines), unlike the Stage 2–5 and track badges that carry soon:true. Separately, KOS.achievements.touch('ja') is called only from recordCheckpoint and mine (js/core/ja.js:248,279), not from record()/finishSession(), so a review that makes the 46th hiragana stable is only noticed on the 30-minute sweep (invariant 163: owner events re-measure).
evidence: js/core/achcatalogue.js:349-361 (registrations without soon), :645-646 (the soon pattern); grep: no caller of KOS.ja.addInput / KOS.ja.mine; js/core/ja.js:87-89 speech:false; touch calls only at js/core/ja.js:248,279.
fix: Mark voice/immersion/sentence-miner soon:true (or do not register them) until their features ship; call KOS.achievements.touch('ja') in finishSession (once per session).

title: VN scene text box is role=button yet contains the Voice, English and From the start buttons (nested interactive controls)
detail: The scene's .k-ja-vn-box is a focusable role='button' ('Next line (click, Enter or Space)') and its descendants are three real buttons. Invariant 67: a card with interactive descendants is not an ARIA button — screen readers flatten the inner buttons into the outer one's name, and Enter on an inner button may also bubble as 'next line'.
evidence: eval (#/ref/ja/1.3, ipad): DIV.k-ja-vn-box role=button tabIndex 0 containing BUTTON[ja.scene-voice], BUTTON[ja.scene-english], BUTTON[ja.scene-again]; Enter/Space/click on the box advance lines correctly. js/core/jaui.js scene() (~line 400-430).
fix: Make 'Next line' its own button (the ▼ marker) and keep the box a plain region with aria-live='polite' for the line; keep the click-anywhere shortcut on the image for pointer users.

title: Lesson Practice tab promises 'reading, then writing and listening … read it, write it, hear the difference', and lists 本 twice as identical chips
detail: The Practice card of a Stage 1 lesson says '14 items · reading, then writing and listening' and 'Each item is introduced, then checked: read it, write it, hear the difference.' The session actually asks one facet per item — Listening first for every word and pattern (see the sibling tie-break entry) — and no Writing until an item has held (it can't on day one by design). title: The F1 checkpoint lesson (F1.8) can never reach Completed: its fourth check reads retrieval over the lesson's concepts, and a checkpoint lesson has none
detail: A lesson without a written prompt has three checks and its fourth slot is 'all three hold' (js/core/mind.js:347-355). For a checkpoint lesson the third evidence check is `retrieval`, computed over `l.concepts` (js/core/mind.js:338-340) — but F1.8 is registered with `concepts: []` (its concepts live on KOS_MIND.CHECKPOINTS.F1.concepts). So retrieval is always false and the shared progress record never gets checks 3–4: after the page is read, the checkpoint is passed and every one of the checkpoint's concepts' cards is rated Good, F1.8 stays 'started' with check [true,true,false,false]. Consequences: the unit can never show 8/8 completed, Mind mastery can never reach 100% (F1.8 caps at 2/3), the desk's 'Lessons' tile tops out at 7/8, and anything reading `completed` (unitState.completed, achievements, Reports) under-counts.

fix: In evidence(), for a checkpoint lesson read the concepts from M().CHECKPOINTS[l.unit].concepts (or its cards) — or treat the checkpoint itself (cards step) as its retrieval; add a smoke110 case that a fully done checkpoint lesson reaches status done.
rootCause: evidence() derives 'retrieval' from l.concepts, which the checkpoint lesson registration leaves empty (js/data/content/mind-f1.js checkpoint lesson)

title: Mind ladder: most F1 concepts can never climb past Recall/Apply — 5 of 16 concepts have no route to any rung above Recall, only 3 can reach Evaluate
detail: The ladder (invariant 137) is derived from four evidence sources: Explain = an explain-back on a lesson whose `main` is the concept, or a checkpoint rubric row; Apply = a check/checkpoint item marked `apply` for the concept; Evaluate = a position on a contested lesson teaching the concept, or an Evaluate rubric row. Enumerating F1's authored content against those rules: premise, deduction, straw-man, false-dilemma and bandwagon have NO Explain, Apply or Evaluate source (they can only ever reach Recall); conclusion, soundness, ad-hominem, slippery-slope reach Recall+Apply only; standard-form has Explain but no Apply; steelman has no Explain (F1.7 is contested, so its prompt is a position). Only induction, charity and steelman can reach Evaluate. Yet every met concept is drawn with four rungs, the desk hero shows 'Evaluate 0%' bars computed over all met concepts and 'furthest' needs half the met concepts on a rung — so a learner who does every piece of F1 perfectly still sees Explain ≈ 38%, Evaluate ≈ 19% and four-rung ladders that cannot be completed, with no hint why.
evidence: eval over KOS_MIND (slot 11): 'premise E[] A[] V[]', 'deduction E[] A[] V[]', 'straw-man E[] A[] V[]', 'false-dilemma E[] A[] V[]', 'bandwagon E[] A[] V[]', 'soundness E[] A[F1.3#2] V[]', 'standard-form E[F1.2] A[] V[]', 'steelman E[] A[F1.7#1] V[F1.7,cp]'; rules in js/core/mind.js:278-318 (ladder); hero bars js/modules/mind.js:66-72; furthest js/core/mind.js:497-503
fix: Either author a route for every rung of every concept (apply items for each fallacy/premise/deduction; explain-back key points or checkpoint rubric rows for the rest), or let a concept declare which rungs it has (`rungs: ['Recall','Apply']`) and draw/count only those, computing the hero bars and 'furthest' over reachable rungs. smoke110 should assert every concept has a source for every rung it shows.
rootCause: Ladder rules require per-concept evidence sources that the F1 content file only provides for the lesson 'main' concepts; nothing checks reachability.

title: Evaluate is lost whenever a position is revised: the revise sheet starts with an empty objection/reply and the ladder reads only the latest version
detail: ladder() grants Evaluate from `latest(lid)` having both objection and reply (js/core/mind.js:308-312). The position sheet pre-fills answer, confidence and reason from the previous version but always starts objection and reply as '' (js/modules/mindrun.js:96 `objection: "", reply: ""`), and the objection <details> is closed. So a learner who answered an objection in v1 and later revises (e.g. a revisit's 'Revise', or nudging confidence) without retyping it drops the concept back below Evaluate — for every concept the contested lesson teaches (F1.7: steelman AND charity). The saved card then shows the ladder without Evaluate and no message says it was lost. An 'earned' rung going away on an unrelated edit contradicts 'every rung comes from evidence' (the earlier evidence still exists in version history).
evidence: eval (slot 11): takePosition('F1.7',{answer:1,objection:'o',reply:'y'}) → ladder('steelman').rungs[3] true, ladder('charity').rungs[3] true; then takePosition('F1.7',{answer:1,conf:60,reason:'r2'}) (what the revise sheet sends when the objection is not retyped) → ladder('steelman').rungs[3] false
fix: Evaluate should hold if ANY version (or any non-retired position) has an objection answered; and pre-fill the revise sheet's objection/reply from the previous version (open the details when present).
rootCause: ladder uses only the latest version; position() sheet does not carry the objection forward

title: Checkpoint pays 50 XP / 12 gold / +4 HP and marks itself passed with nothing right; a retake then erases the Explain/Evaluate rungs it gave
detail: recordCheckpoint() always sets doneAt and pays the first time (js/core/mind.js:382-405); the UI's only gate is one non-empty synthesis bullet (js/modules/mind.js:562). Cards are self-marked 'Had it/Not quite' and apply scenarios can all be wrong — 0 of 8 cards, 0 of 3 scenarios, 0 rubric points and a one-character bullet still pay the full checkpoint reward and tick F1.8's 'Check passed'. (Japanese's checkpoint requires 80% in every skill; the Mind plan's 'unit checkpoint 50/12/+4' reads as a passed checkpoint.) Separately, Retake overwrites `apply` and `synth.ticks` wholesale, so a retake with fewer rubric ticks removes Explain (argument, hidden-premise) and Evaluate (induction, steelman) that the first attempt earned.
evidence: eval (slot 11): recordCheckpoint('F1',{cards:0,apply:{},synth:{bullets:['x'],ticks:{0:true,2:true}}}) → {paid:true}, governor 0/0 → 50/12; ledger [F1.8,{kind:'checkpoint',first:true},{xp:50,gold:12}]; ladder('argument').rungs[1] true, ladder('induction').rungs[3] true; retake recordCheckpoint('F1',{synth:{bullets:['y'],ticks:{}}}) → both false
fix: Define a pass rule (e.g. ≥ 2 of 3 scenarios right and ≥ half the rubric) and pay only on the first PASS, saying what is missing otherwise; keep the best attempt (merge apply/ticks by OR, or store attempts and read the best) so a retake never lowers a rung.
rootCause: recordCheckpoint has no pass condition and replaces the record on every attempt

title: Apply and Explain rungs are earned without showing understanding: Apply after the check has revealed the answer, Explain from one one-character bullet
detail: Leniency of the derived ladder with thin evidence: (1) Apply = 'a scenario answered right'. A wrong answer immediately marks the right option '✓ Right' (js/modules/mindtopic.js:103-106) and offers 'Next, and come back to this'; coming back, clicking the option that was just revealed records ok:true (answerCheck keeps the first ok) and the concept reaches Apply — so every Apply rung (and the check pass that pays 12 XP) can be had by guessing once. (2) Explain = ≥60% of key points self-ticked; the text itself is not checked at all, so a single bullet 'x' with 3 of 4 ticks reaches Explain, and the explain-back can be written before a single page is read.
evidence: eval (slot 11): answerCheck('F1.3',3,0) → ok:false, ladder('validity').apply 0; answerCheck('F1.3',3,1) → ok:true, apply 1, rungs [F,F,T,F]; saveExplain('F1.3',['x'],{0:1,1:1,2:1}) → {reached:true,ticked:3,of:4} with evidence('F1.3').read 0 of 6
fix: Count Apply only when the scenario is right at the FIRST attempt of a visit (or on a later day, with the answer not revealed in the same session); for a retried item show 'Right, but it counts next time'. For Explain require a minimum (e.g. ≥ 3 bullets or ~20 words) before ticks count, and order the prompt after the pages.
rootCause: answerCheck records ok on any later right answer; saveExplain trusts ticks with no text threshold

title: Checkpoint Argument Mapper: every claim starts as 'conclusion', the warning says 'Two conclusions' for five, and an untouched map still earns 'First argument mapped'

'Next · the synthesis' accepts the map as it is, and milestones() counts any stored map as 'First argument mapped' (js/core/mind.js:509) — so pressing Next without moving anything earns the milestone. Nothing compares the learner's map with the model map (only an optional 'Compare' sheet).

title: Practice Log work dialog reopens itself after every action and stacks on each redraw (#/creatives/log/<id>)
detail: Saving from the Writing Desk, a drill or Add your work lands on #/creatives/log/<id>, whose render schedules openWork(id). Any KOS.rerender() while that route is current (the dialog's own 'Take out of Portfolio', the Promote dialog's 'Promote', or any background redraw) draws the page again and opens the work dialog AGAIN. Repro: go to #/creatives, then #/creatives/log/<id>; click 'Take out of Portfolio' -> the dialog closes and immediately re-opens (now showing 'Promote…'). KOS.rerender() with it open -> two identical stacked dialogs (10 buttons). The route never drops the id, so the user cannot act on the work without it bouncing back.
evidence: eval: after cr.promote click count of [data-ui="cr.dialog"] stays 1 with button now 'Promote…'; after KOS.rerender() count 1 -> 2; js/modules/creatives.js:567 'if (wid && CR().work(wid)) setTimeout(function () { openWork(wid); }, 0);' inside logPage; :542 and :559 call d.close(); KOS.rerender(); landing routes js/modules/crwrite.js:147, crdrills.js:85, creatives.js:620

rootCause: Render-time side effect: logPage opens a dialog from the route arg on every render, and the route keeps the id.
